title: Add cache clean all for tool caches
description:
## Summary

Adds `ir cache clean --all` so users can clear `ir`'s own cache along with the pak/pkgcache, renv, and reticulate caches used during dependency and Python environment resolution.

This is useful when resolver/tooling state needs a full reset. External cache locations are resolved from R at runtime, after R startup files and environment setup have run, instead of hardcoding those paths in Rust.

## User-facing changes

- Adds `ir cache clean --all`.
- Clears the `ir`, pak/pkgcache, renv, reticulate, and legacy reticulate caches.
- Prints diagnostics for each cache path, including whether it was found, cleared, and how many files were removed.
- Updates cache command help and cache documentation.

## Internal changes

- Adds `driver/cache-clean.R` for R-owned cache path resolution and deletion.
- Embeds that R script in the binary and runs it through `Rscript` from the cache command.
- Keeps Rust responsible for the Rust-owned `ir` cache only.
- Adds CLI regression coverage for direct envvar cache settings and cache envvars set by `R_PROFILE_USER`.

title: Reuse renv artifacts across IR cache roots
description:
Installing the same package artifact under different `IR_CACHE_DIR` roots created separate renv entries because the artifact hash included the root path. A public CLI reproduction with two roots sharing one temporary renv cache grew from one installed entry to two. Equivalent artifacts now reuse one entry across roots.

Artifact identity retains the selected source or binary, content metadata, source subdirectory, full R version, and platform. Remote artifacts without a content checksum, URL validator, or source revision get a fresh installation when resolved again, without adding an installed-package cache entry. Downloads remain partitioned by IR root and resolved artifact set.

IR locks each writable renv cache root through restore and copies packages into new libraries. Completed libraries therefore survive cache-entry replacement or removal and cleaning another IR root. These independent copies use additional disk space. Locks coordinate IR processes; external writers and owners of read-only cache roots must keep entries stable during copying. Existing entries and libraries are not deleted or migrated, and the cache documentation describes cleanup separately.

Internally, add `filelock` to resolver tooling and use disposable renv and pak caches by default in CLI tests, with explicit cache reuse in CI. Public regressions cover cross-root reuse, deterministic concurrent installs, failed and killed installers, existing-library usability, changed content, source subdirectories, and cache permission boundaries.

title: Fix PPM snapshot URLs using the all repository
description:
`--exclude-newer` can fail during dependency resolution when pak returns a PPM URL such as `https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/__linux__/noble/2024-02-01`, even for scripts that only use CRAN packages. Accept both `/cran/` and `/all/` when deriving the dated Bioconductor mirror, preserving the repository host selected by pak.

Extend the public CLI regression coverage to source and Linux binary URLs for both repository names. The fixture exercises Linux repository selection on every platform and checks the complete CRAN and Bioconductor repository set passed to the installer, along with the existing cache reuse behavior.

Addresses the README failure reported in #159.

title: Install missing R versions with rig in user mode
description:
IR can now use rig to install a missing R version in user mode. If no R selector is supplied and `Rscript` is absent from `PATH`, it selects `release`. This lets IR start with rig alone, without an existing R installation.

IR reuses a matching installed R before downloading and retains the existing selector precedence. Missing versions are resolved using the same version requirements and `exclude-newer` minor-version limits, then installed in rig's default or configured directories. These installations persist outside IR's cache and survive `ir cache clean`. Installation leaves the default R and shell PATH unchanged; explicit `--rscript` and `IR_RSCRIPT` selections remain authoritative.

Internally, IR reads user installations and available releases through rig's JSON output, excludes development builds from broad requirements, checks returned numeric versions, and reports rig failures directly. Public CLI regressions cover installation, reuse, no-R startup, ranges, snapshot dates, Quarto selection, and failure handling. Documentation and the quickstart snapshot describe the new behavior.

This is a draft because automatic installation requires the `--no-default` and `--without-path` flags from r-lib/rig#490, currently available in development rig 0.11.1-dev rather than released rig 0.11.0. Existing installed-version selection still works with older rig.

Validation:

- `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS=2 scripts/check.sh` passed: rustfmt, Clippy with warnings denied, and all 234 tests.
- Red/green public CLI regressions; all 44 selection and installation tests pass.
- Native macOS arm64 smoke tests with rig `17bcb7f`: fresh temporary homes, no Rscript on PATH, automatic R 4.6.1 installation with jsonlite, explicit frontmatter R 4.4.3 installation, and reuse on second invocation. Confirmed rig's default directories, unchanged default R and shell profiles, and R installations surviving `ir cache clean`.
- Native run/render selection test passed with the installed rig 0.10.0 and R 4.4.3.
- Independent source review completed; no remaining findings. Linux and Windows were not tested locally.

title: Prefer compatible package binaries by default
description:
A new CRAN release can be available as source for days, sometimes up to a week, before its pre-built binaries are ready. During that gap, IR currently picks the newest version. I recently ran into this with DuckDB: IR started a slow source build even though an older compatible binary was available.

This PR makes IR prefer compatible binaries, including older versions, for ordinary package requests and their dependencies. Source-only packages can still install alongside binaries.

Set `IR_PREFER_BINARIES=0` to keep prioritizing newer versions. This does not force source installation. Exact pins, minimum versions, and explicit Git, local, URL, or source requests still control what IR installs. MCP Console gets the new default automatically, without configuration changes.

IR still uses pak to resolve dependencies and renv to install them:

- Ordinary requests go into a temporary `DESCRIPTION` file with a unique package name so pak applies its binary preference to requested packages too. This uses pak's public API and adds no pkgdepends dependency or vendored solver code.
- IR passes the selected versions and URLs to `renv::restore()`, preserving the chosen binary through installation.
- If a binary download returns HTTP 404 or 410, IR asks pak to resolve once more using source for that package. pak recalculates the dependencies for the source version. Other errors remain visible. IR may use source even when another older binary could work.
- Cache keys include the binary preference and selected artifacts. Unset and `1` share cached resolutions; `0` is separate. Old plans and incomplete installations are bypassed.

Downloaded archives stay under IR's resolver lock. renv's installed-package cache remains shared, with artifact keys scoped to the IR cache root so concurrent runs using separate roots cannot replace each other's entries.

Local repository tests reproduce the release-lag case: a 1.0.0 binary, a 2.0.0 source release, and a source-only dependency. They check the installed artifact, constraints, fallback, and cache reuse. A synchronized regression also replaces a cached binary during installation and checks that IR still produces a complete library. Documentation includes opt-out examples and a release note about the default and cache transition.

With renv 1.3.0 in an isolated library, `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS=2 scripts/check.sh` passed on macOS: formatting, Clippy, and all 222 tests, with none skipped. Quarto render tests share a nextest group to avoid concurrent writes to Quarto’s Sass cache.

title: Add core script initializer
description:
## Summary

Adds `ir init --file FILE` to turn an existing R script into a self-describing, executable ir script. This separates the core initializer from the project-provenance work in #154 so the in-place rewrite and static dependency discovery can be reviewed and released independently. The branch is based directly on `main`.

Closes #149.

## User-facing changes

- Statically discovers direct package uses, omits packages supplied by the active R, and writes quoted bare package references.
- Records the active R requirement, `isolated: true`, and the current UTC `exclude-newer` date.
- Replaces any existing shebang with `#!/usr/bin/env -S ir run` and makes the script executable on Unix.
- Refuses existing or malformed ir frontmatter, UTF-8 byte order marks, symbolic links, and non-regular files without modifying them.
- Stages the replacement beside the source, syncs it, rechecks the source contents and current permissions, and atomically replaces the file.

Static analysis cannot find package names computed at runtime, so users should inspect the generated metadata.

## Scope

This PR deliberately does not inspect `renv.lock`, pin installed package versions, or preserve repository or remote-source provenance. A nearby lockfile is ignored, and a public CLI regression covers that boundary. It does not add `--no-project`, project initialization, or Quarto initialization. Project-aware version and source conversion will be separate follow-up changes.

Concurrent-edit detection covers changes between the initial read and the final pre-rename recheck. Portable filesystems do not provide a content-aware compare-and-replace operation, so a writer racing the final atomic rename itself is outside this command's concurrency contract.

## Internal changes

- Embeds a small R driver for `renv::dependencies()` static scanning and active-R classification.
- Reuses the existing tooling restart and crash-retry helpers, with private temporary result files.
- Adds public CLI coverage for generated metadata, R release channels, file preservation, atomic replacement checks, permissions, symbolic links, line endings, direct execution, errors, help output, and the explicit lockfile boundary.

title: Initialize existing R scripts in place
description:
## Why

Existing R scripts currently need to be annotated by hand before `ir` can run them as self-describing files. This adds a direct conversion path while keeping the script itself as the dependency manifest.

Closes #149.

## User-facing changes

- Adds `ir init --file FILE` to annotate an existing `.R` file in place. `--no-project` skips renv project discovery.
- Statically finds direct package uses, omits packages supplied by R, and borrows matching versions and supported source references from the nearest `renv.lock` when present.
- Validates CRAN and Bioconductor repository provenance before converting locked packages to inline references and preserves portable Git sources, including SSH URLs with user information.
- Quotes generated package references so YAML-sensitive source metadata round-trips unchanged.
- Records the inspecting Rscript's major and minor as a minimum R version, enables isolation, and sets `exclude-newer` to the current UTC date.
- Adds the portable `ir run` shebang when needed and makes initialized scripts executable on Unix.
- Preserves the existing script body byte-for-byte through an atomic replacement, aborts if the file changes during dependency discovery, and fails without modifying the file when its dependencies or metadata cannot be represented.

## Internal changes

- Adds a dedicated embedded R initialization driver built on the existing tooling bootstrap and resolver lock.
- Shares byte-level shebang and frontmatter boundary detection with the script reader.
- Adds public CLI coverage for dependency discovery, renv source provenance, YAML serialization, generated metadata, concurrent edits, atomic rewrite behavior, line endings, executable mode, and direct execution.

title: Default RETICULATE_PYTHON to managed for ir run
description:
## Summary

`ir run` now sets an otherwise-unset `RETICULATE_PYTHON` to `managed` when a script has no Python metadata. This lets Python-using R packages declare their requirements with `reticulate::py_require()` without reticulate selecting an ambient Python environment first.

Explicit `RETICULATE_PYTHON` values remain unchanged. Scripts with `python-packages` or `python-version` continue to use the concrete Python executable resolved by ir.

## User-facing changes

- Metadata-free `ir run` scripts now default to reticulate's managed Python environment.
- Users can keep another Python selection by setting `RETICULATE_PYTHON` explicitly.
- The run guide and quickstart describe the default and its override. This change does not alter `ir render` or `ir preview`.

## Internal changes

- The shared R script launch path supplies the managed default only when ir did not resolve Python and the caller did not set `RETICULATE_PYTHON`.
- Public CLI coverage verifies both the managed default and preservation of an explicit caller selection.

title: Require renv 1.2.0 for resolver tooling
description:
## Summary

`ir` passed effective repositories to `renv::use()` but accepted any installed `renv` version. Before `renv` 1.2.0, `repos` was not a formal argument to `use()`, so the repository vector was interpreted as a package specification and dependency resolution failed with `the condition has length > 1`.

Require `renv` 1.2.0 or newer when preparing ir's private resolver tooling. Older ambient copies are replaced before package materialization. The minimum also becomes part of the private tooling cache key.

A public CLI regression covers `ir run` with ambient `renv` 1.1.7. `scripts/check.sh` passes with all 206 tests.

## User-facing changes

Scripts and documents that declare R packages now work when the user's library contains `renv` older than 1.2.0. The first resolution may install a compatible version into ir's private tooling cache.

## Internal changes

- Add version metadata to the resolver tooling fixture.
- Test that old ambient `renv` is replaced before repositories are passed to `renv::use()`.

Fixes #148

title: Publish r-lib-ir wheels to PyPI
description:
## Summary

Make `ir` installable from PyPI with `uv tool install r-lib-ir`, which installs both `ir` and `rx` without a Python wrapper. Extend the tag-driven release so GitHub and PyPI artifacts use the same Cargo version and a failed PyPI publication stops the release before the post-release development-version commit.

## User-facing changes

- Add PyPI metadata for binary-only Maturin wheels under the package name `r-lib-ir`.
- Publish wheels for macOS ARM and x86, manylinux ARM and x86, and Windows x86.
- Document the `uv` installation path and its two installed commands.
- Describe `ir` and `rx` together in the package metadata.

## Internal changes

- Build and install a local wheel in Linux CI, then verify the installed `ir` and `rx` versions.
- Build and install-test every release wheel on its native platform before publishing the GitHub Release.
- Require the release tag to match the Cargo package version, then publish the wheel artifacts to PyPI with OIDC.
- Document the one-time Trusted Publisher setup and recovery limits for a partial PyPI upload.

## Notes

The first PyPI release requires the `pypi` GitHub environment and the pending Trusted Publisher described in `RELEASE.md`. The workflow publishes wheels only, without a source distribution.

title: Cache Python resolutions by uv storage paths
description:
## Summary

Reuse cached Python resolutions when `UV_CACHE_DIR` or `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR` is set. Previously, any nonempty `UV_*` variable disabled cache reuse, even though these two variables are stable path inputs.

Including their effective paths in the cache key preserves reuse for identical settings while resolving again when either uv storage location changes.

## User-facing changes

- Python dependencies no longer resolve again on every run solely because `UV_CACHE_DIR` or `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR` is set.
- Changing either path uses a separate cached resolution, so an interpreter from another uv storage location is not reused.

## Internal changes

- Treat the two uv path variables as cache-key inputs while continuing to make other nonempty `UV_*` variables and `RETICULATE_UV` bypass the cache.
- Resolve relative uv paths against the current working directory before hashing them.
- Add public `ir run` coverage for reuse and isolation across multiple uv path combinations.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --no-fail-fast -j 4` (205 passed)

title: Prevent local-source package installation with IR_NO_LOCAL_SOURCES
description:
## Summary

Add an environment-only control for workflows that should not execute R package installation code from local file-system sources. When `IR_NO_LOCAL_SOURCES` is nonempty, IR inspects pak's complete resolved manifest immediately before renv materialises packages and reports any local sources instead of installing them.

Cached resolutions and materialised libraries remain reusable across restricted and unrestricted invocations because those paths do not run package installation code. The option intentionally does not verify where packages already present in a reused library were originally resolved.

This feature is motivated by the dynamic environment resolution feature in [`mcp-console`](https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console). Since resolution runs outside the sandbox, this closes a loophole where clients could execute arbritray code outside the sandbox by requesting installation of local packages. There is a mitigation in `mcp-console` already, but it's simpler to enforce here, where we have easy access to the fully resolved pak manifest. 

## User-facing changes

- Prevent installs from direct or transitive local package refs, `file:` URLs, and `file:` repositories.
- Report each offending package and source before renv materialises the library.
- Preserve normal resolution-marker and materialised-library reuse across policy modes.
- Document `IR_NO_LOCAL_SOURCES`; no CLI option is added.

## Internal changes

- Classify pak manifest rows as local from their resolved type and `file:` source or mirror locators.
- Have Rust pass the selected policy to the resolver as an internal Rscript argument, so startup profiles cannot disable it before a cold materialisation.
- Validate after the full dependency set is resolved and only on the path that calls renv.
- Cover direct, transitive, file-repository, remote-source, startup-profile, cached-resolution, Rscript-wrapper, and completed-library behavior through the public CLI.

title: Automate the release process
description:
## Summary

Add a small, linear release command so maintainers do not need to coordinate version commits, CI, tagging, publication checks, artifact verification, and the development-version reset by hand.

## User-facing changes

- Add `scripts/release.sh VERSION` for stable releases from a clean, up-to-date `main` checkout on supported macOS and Linux hosts.
- Run the complete local check, push the stable version, watch its exact CI run, create the annotated tag, and watch the tag-driven release workflow.
- Download and checksum the current host's archive, smoke-test `ir`, `rx`, and a short R execution, then restore `VERSION+dev` and watch its CI run.
- Document prerequisites, the release sequence, and manual recovery after a failure in `RELEASE.md`.

## Internal changes

- Keep the script to a single fail-fast path with no automatic recovery state machine.
- Require both `origin` fetch and push URLs to resolve to `r-lib/ir` before changing files.
- Add two black-box tests using real local Git repositories and a small GitHub shim, covering invalid input and the complete release sequence.

## Notes

The complete local check passes with 198 tests. The release script also passes Bash syntax and ShellCheck validation.

title: Cache network-backed resolutions and add refresh
description:
## Summary

Cache dependency graphs that pak resolves to network-backed package sources, so a second invocation of the same script can reuse the resolved library without launching R or performing another network operation.

Previously, the cache policy classified the user’s input ref before resolution. That excluded remote refs such as `r-xla/anvl` and could not account for transitive or mixed local/network graphs. This change lets pak resolve the graph once, then bases the cache policy on pak’s resolved source locations.

## User-facing changes

- Reuse warm resolutions for any graph containing a network-backed source, including registry snapshots, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, git, URL, SCP-style SSH, transitive remote dependencies, and mixed local/network graphs.
- Add `--refresh` to `run`, `render`, `preview`, `tool run`, `rx`, and `tool install`.
- Support nonempty `IR_REFRESH` as the environment-level refresh control.
- Treat `IR_LATEST_RESOLUTION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS=0` as an unconditional miss for time-bounded markers, including markers written during the current second.
- Continue resolving local-only graphs and refs with pak query modifiers on every invocation.
- Preserve the previous warm result when a refresh fails.

## Internal changes

- Remove custom Rust and R parsing of user package refs for cache policy decisions.
- Use pak’s resolved `sources`, `mirror`, and `params` fields to identify network-backed graphs and explicit query modifiers.
- Apply one expiring-marker policy to every network-backed R graph. `exclude-newer` remains part of the cache key but no longer makes a network resolution permanently current.
- Create marker timestamps only after successful materialization.
- Store each tool provider’s timestamp, library path, and package name in an independent marker so providers sharing a dependency set remain coherent across refreshes.
- Bypass both R and Python resolution markers during refresh, including reads after acquiring the resolver lock.
- Use pak’s direct-package result, with a focused pak solve when needed, to identify the primary package for tool metadata.
- Update command help, cache documentation, and public CLI regression coverage.

title: Support additional package repositories
description:
## Summary

Fixes #128 by letting users add CRAN-like package repositories, such as R-universe, before IR's defaults. This lets pak resolve package refs whose dependencies are published outside CRAN and Bioconductor.

## User-facing changes

- Add repeatable `--repo` options to run, render, preview, rx, and tool commands, plus `repos` / `ir.repos` frontmatter.
- Keep command-line repositories before frontmatter and default repositories. `exclude-newer` still dates the defaults; additional repositories remain live.
- Keep Git repositories as pak package refs, not repository options.

## Internal changes

- Pass pak's ordered effective repository set to renv and preserve multi-URL repository specs.
- Include repositories in resolution keys, refresh live repositories after 24 hours, and use pak artifact identities to avoid stale same-version builds.
- Preserve credential-free repository options in installed-tool recovery commands.

title: Support Bioconductor repositories
description:
## Summary

Fixes #143 by passing pak's effective repository set to renv during materialization. This lets Bioconductor packages resolve and install through the normal bare-package interface.

## User-facing changes

- Support commands such as `ir run --with BiocGenerics` without an explicit repository.
- Let pak select the Bioconductor release compatible with the selected R.
- Apply `exclude-newer` to both the default CRAN and Bioconductor PPM snapshots.
- Document Bioconductor usage in the README, website, quickstart, and CLI help.

## Internal changes

- Use the ordered rows from `pak::repo_get()` as renv's repository vector.
- Clear renv's inherited repository override so pak's effective repository set remains authoritative.
- Derive a dated Bioconductor mirror from the resolved PPM CRAN URL.
- Disable renv's pak integration inside IR's resolver until rstudio/renv#2341 is fixed, preserving exact resolved versions.
- Add deterministic local and synthetic CLI regressions plus a Linux smoke test with real `BiocGenerics`.

## Notes

This PR is intentionally independent of #142 and contains no `--repo` or frontmatter `repos` changes.

title: Redirect resolver stdout to stderr
description:
## Summary

- The resolver subprocess (pak/renv) writes package install progress to stdout, which pollutes the script's actual output
- Pipe the resolver's stdout and forward it to stderr so that `ir run script.R | cmd` works cleanly even on first run when packages need to be installed

Fixes #138

## Test plan

- [ ] `IR_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) ir run --with readr -e 'cat("hello\n")' > out.txt 2>/dev/null` — `out.txt` should contain only `hello`
- [ ] `ir run -e 'cat("cached\n")'` still works when packages are already cached
- [ ] Package install progress still visible on stderr when not suppressed

title: Fix missing reticulate installation for Python renders
description:
## Summary

Quarto Jupyter renders with Python metadata could fail when reticulate was not already installed. The resolver passed `reticulate@>=1.41.0` to pak, but pak does not support version ranges in package refs.

## User-facing changes

- Install reticulate from the tooling repository using a plain package ref when it is missing.
- Keep the existing minimum version check at 1.41.0.

## Internal changes

- Add an isolated CLI regression test that renders a Jupyter Quarto document without ambient reticulate and verifies the private tooling install path.

Fixes #135

title: Fix and test documented dependency environments
description:
## Summary

Fixes #137 by replacing unsupported pak minimum-version refs in the user-facing examples with realistic dated environments. The main example leaves dplyr unpinned, pins tidyr to 1.3.1, and uses the 2024-02-01 snapshot to select dplyr and transitive dependencies.

The same snapshot now limits `r-version: ">= 4.3"` to R minor versions released by that date, so an installed R-devel is not selected implicitly.

## User-facing changes

- Update the README, script, Quarto, quickstart, and Rustdoc examples to use supported package refs.
- Document that pak does not currently resolve minimum-version refs.
- Limit R requirements that can match multiple minor versions to released R versions, and apply `exclude-newer` to R selection as well as package resolution.
- Keep exact R selectors and explicit Rscript selections authoritative.

## Internal changes

- Add release- and date-aware R selection with public CLI regression coverage.
- Add end-to-end tests that extract and execute the affected published R and Quarto examples, checking R and package versions, isolation, and rendered output.
- Use R 4.3 for the non-default test runtime and warm the documented snapshot packages in development and CI setup.

title: Install selected R versions on demand
description:
## Summary

`ir` now uses the development version of rig to install missing selected R versions into `<IR_CACHE_DIR>/rig` in user mode. This lets scripts and documents select R versions without requiring every version to be installed system-wide or requiring administrator access.

## User-facing changes

- Numeric versions, major versions, comparisons, `release`, `oldrel`, `oldrel/N`, `devel`, and `next` can be installed automatically when absent.
- Release-style selectors resolve to a concrete version once per cache so later runs reuse the same R version.
- The installation and development setup scripts install or recommend a rig build with public user-mode support.
- Generated tool launchers report an exact reinstall command if their selected R executable or tool library has been removed.
- The documentation explains cache cleanup and the per-user integration state rig may create on macOS and Windows.

## Internal changes

- Private rig operations use isolated install, binary, home, and temporary directories while retaining support for ambient rig-managed R installations.
- A cache lock serializes private R installation, and symbolic selector resolutions are cached as concrete versions.
- Regression coverage includes concurrent installs, selector boundaries, environment isolation, setup scripts, launcher recovery, and real rig runs on disposable GitHub-hosted macOS, Linux, and Windows runners.

Local validation passed `scripts/check.sh` with 205 tests, plus Linux and Windows cross-target checks.

title: Draft ir 0.1.0 release announcement
description:
## Summary
Drafts a Posit Open Source announcement for the first public release of `ir`, so the release has a reviewable public narrative before publication. The post positions `ir` around two user workflows: self-describing R/Quarto files and command-line tools distributed through R packages, while clarifying how `ir` sits alongside `rig`, `pak`, and `renv`.

## User-facing changes
- Adds `blog-post-ir-release-draft.md` with frontmatter for the Posit Open Source site.
- Introduces `ir run` and `ir render` for scripts and Quarto documents that declare their runtime requirements in YAML metadata.
- Explains cached package libraries, isolation, `exclude-newer`, R selection, optional Python metadata, and Quarto integration.
- Presents `rx` as the short alias for `ir tool run`, covers package `exec/` tools and `Rapp` apps, and shows persistent launchers through `ir tool install`.
- Includes install commands, project links, and a call for feedback from early users.

## Internal changes
- Documentation-only change; no CLI or runtime behavior changes.
- The draft describes how `ir` uses existing tools such as `pak`, `renv`, `rig`, reticulate/uv, and Quarto as part of the release messaging.

title: Add per-package dependency specs (`r-pkgs` and structured `--with`)
description:
Closes #28.

Generalises per-package `Suggests` resolution into a full pak/remotes-style **per-package `dependencies` spec**, selectable both in frontmatter and on the command line. This supersedes the original `--with-suggests` flag (now removed), following the discussion below.

## Frontmatter

`r-pkgs:` is the canonical package-list key (`dependencies:` is kept as an alias). Each entry is a plain ref or a `{name, dependencies}` mapping carrying its own dependency-type policy:

```r
#| r-pkgs:
#|   - dplyr
#|   - {name: tidyr, dependencies: [suggests]}
#|   - {name: cli, dependencies: [imports, enhances]}
```

## Command line

`--with` takes the same structured spec as YAML, so dependency types can be chosen per package without editing the script:

```sh
ir run --with '{name: cli, dependencies: [suggests, enhances]}' -e 'library(cli)'
ir tool run --with '{name: btw, dependencies: true}' btw
```

## Semantics

A `dependencies` value **replaces** the default for that package, mirroring pak/remotes:

| `dependencies`            | types followed for that package                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| omitted / `na`            | hard (`Depends`, `Imports`, `LinkingTo`)         |
| `true`                    | hard + `Suggests`                                |
| `false`                   | none                                             |
| a list, e.g. `[suggests]` | exactly the listed types                         |
| `hard` / `soft` / `all`   | type groups                                      |

The listed types apply only to that package; transitive dependencies always follow hard deps (so `[suggests]` pulls a package's direct `Suggests`, not the Suggests of those Suggests). Unavailable `Suggests`/`Enhances` are skipped, mirroring `install.packages(dependencies = TRUE)`. Because the list replaces the default, `[suggests]` drops the package's own `Imports` — use `[hard, suggests]` or `true` to keep them.

## How it works

`pkgdepends` has no per-ref `dependencies` parameter, so per-package types are realised from a **single consistent pak solve**: solve a bounded superset (direct refs follow the union of every requested policy; transitive deps follow hard deps), then graph-prune each package to its own policy using the type-tagged `deps` edge tables pak already attaches to each resolved row. This keeps one consistent solve, and lets unavailable soft dependencies drop naturally — no `available.packages()` pre-filter.

Rust validates dependency-type tokens while parsing arguments, so malformed specs fail fast before any R session starts. The resolver stdin protocol carries `ref` or `ref<TAB>types`; the resolution-cache key folds each ref's policy and is unchanged for plain-ref runs, so existing cache entries stay valid.

## Tests

Following the fixture-based e2e style from #39:

- `run_with_structured_dep_spec_selects_dependency_types` — real end-to-end: `--with cachem` resolves cachem's `Imports` (`fastmap`) but not `testthat`, while `--with '{name: cachem, dependencies: [suggests]}'` materialises `testthat` and drops `fastmap`, exercising replace semantics. Both runs share a cache directory.
- `run_frontmatter_structured_dep_spec_pulls_suggests` — the same through a `{name, dependencies}` entry under both `r-pkgs:` and the `dependencies:` alias.
- `run_structured_dep_spec_validation_fails_fast` — malformed specs (unknown type, missing `name`, unknown key, malformed YAML) error before resolving.

Help snapshots regenerated; README and `docs/` updated.

title: Cover `ir run --r-version` selection in end-to-end tests
description:
The end-to-end fixtures added in #39 all run under the default R, so the version-selection path — which resolves through rig — had no real coverage. There are two ways to select an R version, on separate code paths:

- `--r-version` on the command line. A Quarto document is rendered under an explicitly requested, non-default R, asserting both the R version knitr ran under and that the resolved library was injected.
- `r-version` in a script's `#|` frontmatter. An `.R` script that pins its own R version runs straight through (no quarto), asserting the same.

Both reuse the in-R marker convention from the existing fixtures, so the library check resolves platform symlinks (e.g. macOS `/private`) on both sides instead of comparing paths in Rust.

The tests are gated on `IR_TEST_R_VERSION`: unset, they skip, so they are a no-op for contributors without rig and a second R installed.

## CI

`ir run` resolves a version request through rig, which `r-lib/actions/setup-r` does not provide, so the `test` job now installs rig and a second R (4.4.3) on Linux and macOS alongside the existing toolchain. `IR_RSCRIPT` is pinned to the setup-r `Rscript` before rig is installed: on Linux `rig add` makes its R the default and links it into `/usr/local/bin`, which would otherwise shadow the intended default on `PATH`.

The `windows-latest` job is unchanged here. `ir run` on Windows still resolves a `\?\` verbatim path that quarto cannot stat; that is tracked in #32 and fixed separately, and the Windows version-selection provisioning lands with that fix. The `.R` frontmatter test would already pass on Windows once provisioned — it never touches quarto.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `cargo test` without `IR_TEST_R_VERSION` — the version tests skip, the rest of the suite is unchanged
- [ ] On Linux/macOS with rig and a non-default R provisioned — both version tests run under the requested R and pass

title: Build binaries in CI
description:
Closes #30.

Ship pre-built `ir` binaries so users can install without a Rust toolchain.

## Approach

Hand-rolled, in the style of [`posit-dev/mcp-repl`](https://github.com/posit-dev/mcp-repl): a tag-driven GitHub Actions release workflow using the plain `gh` CLI (no third-party actions, no `cargo-dist`, no signing secrets), plus our own install scripts for the one-line `curl | sh` UX. `ir` is a pure-Rust binary that only shells out to R/rig/quarto at runtime, so every target builds natively with a plain `cargo build --release` — no cross-compilation.

(For contrast: `posit-dev/air` uses cargo-dist and `posit-dev/ark` is hand-rolled but heavyweight because it *embeds* R — neither complication applies here. The installers target `~/.local/bin`, the same family of paths `ir tool install` already uses.)

## What's included

**`.github/workflows/release.yml`**
- Triggers on `v*` tag push (and `workflow_dispatch` to build artifacts, or to re-publish an existing tag). No rolling `dev` release.
- `build` matrix over 5 targets on native runners, each with `--locked`, an `ir --help` smoke test, and `tar.gz`/`zip` packaging:

  | Target | Runner |
  | --- | --- |
  | `aarch64-apple-darwin` | `macos-14` |
  | `x86_64-apple-darwin` | `macos-15-intel` |
  | `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | `ubuntu-22.04` |
  | `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` | `ubuntu-22.04-arm` |
  | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | `windows-2022` |

- `publish` job (only when a tag is known) writes an aggregated `SHA256SUMS.txt` and creates the Release via `gh`; prerelease tags (`vX.Y.Z-rc1`) are marked accordingly.

**`scripts/install.sh` / `scripts/install.ps1`**
- One-line install that detects platform, downloads the latest archive, verifies the binary runs, and installs into `~/.local/bin` (`$HOME\bin` on Windows; override with `IR_INSTALL_DIR`). The shell installer enforces a glibc 2.35 floor.

**`README.md`** — new Install section leading with pre-built binaries; Rust toolchain noted as only needed to build from source.

## Validation
- `actionlint` and `shellcheck` clean.
- End-to-end local test: built `aarch64-apple-darwin`, packaged it exactly as the workflow does, ran `install.sh` against the resulting archive — extract → verify → install succeeded and the installed binary reported `ir 0.1.0`.
- `install.ps1` was not runtime-tested (no PowerShell available locally); it mirrors mcp-repl's working script.

## Notes
- Archives bundle the binary + `README.md`. There's no `LICENSE` file in the repo yet (Cargo.toml declares MIT) — left out of scope here; easy to add to the archive later.
- Windows arm64 omitted (rare); the x64 build runs under emulation. Easy to add if wanted.
- The install URLs point at `main`, so they resolve once this is merged.

title: Add -e and --with flags to ir run
description:
Adds two flags to `ir run`, mirroring and extending Rscript:

- **`-e <expr>`** — evaluate an inline R expression instead of a script file. Repeatable (`-e … -e …`); trailing args flow to `commandArgs(TRUE)`, like `Rscript -e`.
- **`--with <pkg>`** — declare dependencies on the command line. Repeatable, comma-splittable (`--with dplyr,tidyr`), same spec grammar as the `dependencies:` frontmatter. Merged with a script's frontmatter deps; the sole dependency source for `-e`.

```console
$ ir run -e '1 + 1'
$ ir run --with cli -e 'cli::cli_alert_success("hi")'
$ ir run --with 'dplyr>=1.1' --with tidyr script.R
```

### Notes
- `parse_run_args` now treats `-e`/`--with` as first-class `ir`-level flags (the old "first non-`-` arg is the script" heuristic would have misread `-e`'s expression as a path). Other `-…` args are still forwarded to Rscript verbatim.
- Driver merges `--with` specs (passed as argv) with frontmatter deps and tolerates empty frontmatter for the `-e` case.
- Inline `-e` deps come only from `--with`; frontmatter-only directives (`exclude after:`, `R:`) remain file-only.

### Testing
- `cargo test`: 20 CLI tests + R resolution suite pass; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` clean.
- Verified end-to-end against real R: inline eval, multiple `-e` + `commandArgs`, `--with` resolving from CRAN into an isolated cache library, and re-run cache hit.

title: Adopt packages frontmatter syntax
description:
## Summary

Reworks the frontmatter shape before the first public release by using `packages:` for package refs and adding `isolated: true` as explicit YAML metadata. This follows the config-structure concern first encountered in #42 and leaves `dependencies` available as a future name for a pak dependency policy if that idea is revisited.

## User-facing changes

- `packages:` is now the frontmatter key for pak package refs in R scripts and under `ir:` for Quarto documents.
- `isolated: true` in frontmatter disables the user library for the run.
- Unknown valid-YAML keys are ignored so future fields, such as `sys-reqs`, can appear before `ir` supports them.

- Docs, examples, and fixtures now use the new syntax.

title: Add rx shortcut for package tool runs
description:
## Summary

Adds `rx`, a sibling executable for `ir` that behaves as shorthand for `ir tool run`. This gives users a shorter command for one-off package executable runs while keeping the full `ir tool run` interface intact.

## User-facing changes

- Adds `rx [OPTIONS] [ARGS]...` as a public executable installed alongside `ir`.
- Supports the existing tool-run API through `rx`, including `--from`, `--with`, `-w`, `--r-version`, and forwarded tool arguments.
- Updates docs and README examples to show `rx`.
- Updates release archives and installers to include `rx`.

## Internal changes

- Adds a small `rx` wrapper binary that locates sibling `ir` and dispatches through a hidden `ir tool rx` path.
- Shares the existing tool-run parser and execution path between `ir tool run` and `rx`.
- Adds CLI snapshots and regression coverage for `rx` help, version, usage errors, and real package entrypoint execution.

title: Skip the resolver R session on warm cache hits
description:
## Summary
- Move resolution-cache lookup into Rust so warm cache hits can reuse a materialised library before starting the private resolver R session.
- Make Rust own cache-root selection and pass the selected root into the resolver as `IR_CACHE_DIR`, keeping cache markers and resolver output in one tree without an R preflight.
- Keep latest resolution keys stable while storing the current UTC freshness date inside the marker, so stale latest markers refresh in place instead of accumulating one marker per day.

## Why
- The resolver R session has startup cost and startup side effects even when dependencies were already resolved.
- The cache root needs to be available before launching R; otherwise a warm-cache path still pays for R startup just to discover where the cache lives.

## User-facing changes
- Warm `run`, `tool run`, and `tool install` cache hits can skip the first resolver R session entirely.
- `IR_CACHE_DIR` remains authoritative. Without it, `ir` uses process `R_USER_CACHE_DIR`, process `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, or platform defaults and appends `R/ir`; R startup files no longer redirect the `ir` cache.
- `ir cache dir` and `ir cache clean` operate on the same Rust-owned cache tree used by resolver markers and materialised libraries.
- Quarto `rmarkdown` injection remains quiet across cold and warm resolution paths.

## Internal changes
- Added `src/resolve_cache.rs` for resolution marker keying, cache reads, Rscript identity, and primary-package sidecar paths.
- Added SHA-256 and UTC-date dependencies for cache keying and marker freshness.
- Changed resolution markers to store a source/freshness line followed by the materialised library path.
- Added primary-package marker handling so `tool install` can skip the resolver and still know which package `exec/` directory to inspect.
- Added regression coverage for normalized dependency cache keys, latest marker refresh, Rust-owned cache root behavior, warm `tool install`, Rscript wrapper fallback, and quiet Quarto injection.
- Updated cache/config docs to describe the Rust-owned cache root and warm-cache fast path.

title: Support direct executable package tools in ir
description:
## Summary
- Support `ir tool run`, `rx`, and `ir tool install` for package `exec/` entries that are ordinary executables, while preserving the existing Rscript and Rapp dispatch paths.
- Keep package installation delegated to `renv`/`pak`: cache keys use fully resolved package/version/source refs, while install uses the original normalized refs.
- Add an end-to-end dummy package regression covering Bash, Python, sh, Rscript, and Rapp executables for both one-shot runs and installed launchers.
- Update README, package-tool docs, and Quarto fixture comments to match the current executable and resolver behavior.

## User-facing changes
- Package tools can now run and install direct executable scripts from package `exec/`, not only Rscript/Rapp entries.
- `rx`/`ir tool run` docs now describe direct executables and supported installed launchers.

## Internal changes
- Add direct launcher detection/dispatch and installed launcher generation for executable package entries.
- Keep resolved cache identity tied to concrete pak resolution output without reconstructing install refs for renv.

title: Pass pak GitHub refs through to renv use unchanged
description:
## Summary
- Support pak source refs in `ir run` dependencies without collapsing them to plain `package@version` refs before install.
- Preserve source install refs when materialising libraries with `renv::use()`, including direct GitHub refs, GitHub subdirectory refs, transitive source refs, URL/git-family refs, and local package refs.
- Require frontmatter `packages` to be a YAML sequence, or `null`/absent for no dependencies, instead of splitting scalar strings on whitespace.
- Document the supported package-ref, frontmatter, and cache behavior.

## Public behavior
- `packages` and `--with` continue to support ordinary refs such as `pkg`, `pkg>=1.0`, and `pkg==1.2`.
- Frontmatter `packages` is now a structured YAML/JSON value: omit it, set it to `null`, or use a sequence where each entry is one package ref. Scalar strings are rejected.
- `--with` may still be repeated and still accepts comma-separated package refs as a command-line convenience.
- Source refs supported by pak are now treated as first-class install refs. This includes GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, git, URL, HTTP(S), SSH, refs containing `/`, and local refs such as `local::path`, `./path`, or `pkg=local::path`.
- GitHub package refs should be written in pak-style forms such as `github::owner/repo@ref` or `github::owner/repo/subdir@ref`; GitHub browser URLs are not rewritten.
- Transitive source refs returned by pak are also preserved when installing, rather than being rewritten to `package@version`.

## Cache behavior
- Ordinary registry refs still use the warm resolution-marker cache. When the same request is seen again and the marker is current, Rust reuses the cached library path before launching the resolver R session, so pak is not invoked.
- Latest registry resolution markers still refresh after `IR_LATEST_RESOLUTION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` and are refreshed in place. Snapshot resolution with `exclude-newer` remains keyed by the snapshot date.
- Source input refs skip the resolution-marker cache. Each run asks pak to resolve them again so branch heads, URLs, and local package contents can change.
- Materialised libraries are now keyed by the install refs passed to `renv::use()`, R version, and platform. This keeps source refs and versioned refs in distinct cached libraries.
- Source refs are passed to `renv::use()` on each run so renv can refresh source installs; renv may still reuse its own package cache when the resolved source has not changed.

## Internal changes
- The Rust-side resolution cache path builder returns no marker paths for source refs, matching the resolver's fallback behavior.
- The frontmatter parser no longer tokenizes scalar `packages` values; sequence entries are preserved as single refs, including local paths containing spaces.
- CI passes `GITHUB_PAT` into `cargo test` so the GitHub-ref regression can install from GitHub with the workflow token.

title: Clarify CLI help and package-tool wording
description:
## Summary
- Tighten the public help text and docs so `ir run`, `ir render`, and `ir tool` show concrete examples and clearer command descriptions.
- Replace the old `exec/`-centric wording with language that matches current package-tool behavior, including the fact that tool runs resolve package executables from the installed package and support `Rscript` or `Rapp` shebangs.
- Keep the user-facing docs in sync with the CLI snapshots so the reference text matches what `ir` prints.

## Internal changes
- Updated `src/cli.rs` to add `after_help` example blocks and refine the `--from`/package-tool help strings.
- Adjusted the help snapshots under `tests/snapshots/` to lock the new CLI output.
- Made small prose updates in `README.md`, `docs/index.qmd`, and `docs/tools.qmd` to match the revised terminology.

## Notes

title: Apply clap help styling to `ir` CLI
description:
**Summary**

**Notes**

title: Style CLI help section headings with clap colors
description:
## Summary

- Update `ir tool --help` to render its `Tools` section through the helper, keeping the public help output consistent with the existing colored examples blocks.

## Notes

title: Add dark-mode docs styling and colorized CLI reference output
description:
## Summary
- Update the docs site to support light and dark themes, with a dedicated dark stylesheet so the reference pages remain readable in both modes.
- Render the live `ir` help output as colored HTML instead of plain text, so the documentation mirrors the real CLI output more closely and is easier to scan.
- Build the current `ir` binary during docs publishing and expose it to Quarto, instead of downloading a released artifact, so the reference page always reflects the checked-out source.
- Keep the CLI help color-aware in the app itself by enabling clap's automatic color handling.
- Add regression coverage for the docs pages to verify dark-mode styling, colored help rendering, and the build-time wiring used by the reference page.

title: Use compatible R_LIBS_USER tooling before reinstalling resolver packages
description:
## Summary
- Make resolver tooling reuse packages from `R_LIBS_USER` when they are compatible with the selected R minor version instead of always reinstalling them into the private tooling cache.
- This avoids unnecessary installs and reduces failures when users already have usable `pak`, `renv`, or `secretbase` in their user library.
- Keep rejecting user-library packages built against a different R minor version so the resolver still avoids ABI-mismatched tooling.
- Add regression coverage for both paths: compatible user-library tooling is accepted, and incompatible user-library tooling is ignored in favor of installing into the private cache.
- Minor test cleanup: factor executable-bit setup into a shared helper and remove now-unneeded `R_LIBS_USER` overrides in existing R-version selection tests.

Closes #47

title: Normalize docs and fixtures with yamark
description:

title: Honor package launcher metadata in tool runs and installs
description:
## Summary
- Use `#| launcher:` metadata on package apps to rename the command discovered by `rx --from pkg <command>` and the installed launcher name.
- Apply explicit launcher `Rscript` options such as `default-packages`, `vanilla`, `no-environ`, and related flags when running or generating launchers.
- Tighten YAML frontmatter parsing errors by reporting the relevant context for script and launcher metadata.
- Document the new launcher metadata behavior in `docs/tools.qmd` so users can see how package app commands are discovered and installed.

## Notes
- `tool run` now passes launcher metadata through to the runtime environment, including `RAPP_LAUNCHER_NAME`.
- `tool run --from <pkg-ref> <command>` now looks up package executables in the primary resolved package, including metadata-renamed launchers, instead of considering executables from dependency packages.
- `tool install` now preserves the same launcher-specific runtime arguments in generated launcher scripts.
- Added coverage for both `tool run` and `tool install` using launcher metadata.

title: Parse frontmatter as the first YAML document
description:
## Summary

Parse frontmatter by asking saphyr to consume the first YAML document instead of manually scanning for Quarto's closing `---` fence. This removes a fragile line-oriented parser and lets valid YAML document syntax drive the boundary.

## User-facing changes

- `ir run` continues to read dependency metadata from R script frontmatter and Quarto `ir:` metadata.
- Quarto frontmatter is now parsed as the first YAML document in the file, including valid document markers with trailing comments.

## Internal changes

- Replaced Quarto's manual YAML block extraction with full-document reading plus `saphyr_parser::Parser::load(..., false)`.
- Split R-script and Quarto frontmatter parsing into explicit helpers.
- Renamed the R script metadata reader to `read_r_script_frontmatter_to_string`.
- Added a direct `saphyr-parser` dependency so the parser can stop after the first YAML document.

title: Move ref normalization into Rust
description:
## Summary
- Move package ref normalization out of the R resolver and into Rust so the R session stays thinner.
- Keep the resolver focused on pak/renv work while Rust now normalizes `pkg>=...` and `pkg==...` refs before sending them on stdin.
- Preserve the public CLI behavior with a regression test that checks normalized refs share the same resolution cache entry.

## Testing
- `cargo test`
- `cargo check`

title: Use clap for CLI parsing

title: Support Quarto documents in `ir run`
description:
`ir run script.R` resolves a script's `#|` frontmatter dependencies into an isolated, content-addressed library and runs the script against that library and the selected R. Quarto documents had no equivalent.

`ir run` now renders Quarto documents (`.qmd`, `.Rmd`). Dependencies are declared under an `ir:` key in the document's YAML frontmatter, reusing the resolver's existing vocabulary:

```yaml
---
title: "My report"
ir:
  dependencies:
    - dplyr>=1.0
    - gt@1.0
  r-version: ">= 4.0"
  exclude-newer: "2024-01-15"
---
```

`ir run report.qmd` resolves those dependencies into the same cached library used for scripts, then runs `quarto render report.qmd` against that library and the selected R.

## How it works

Phase 1 (resolve + materialise) is unchanged: the `ir:` block produces the identical stdin + env inputs a script produces, so `driver/resolve.R` is untouched. Phase 2 dispatches by extension. `.qmd` and `.Rmd` route to a new `run_quarto`; every other name — including `.R` and extensionless shebang scripts — keeps the existing `run_script` flow.

`run_quarto` sets, on the `quarto render` process:

- `QUARTO_R` — the same Rscript `ir` resolved against, so the document renders with the R it was resolved for. With `r-version`, that is the rig-selected R; `--r-version` overrides the frontmatter and applies here too. Left unset for a bare `Rscript` so quarto resolves it on PATH (the same binary), avoiding quarto's "Specified QUARTO_R does not exist" warning.
- `R_LIBS` — the materialised library, only when dependencies resolved.
- `QUARTO_KNITR_RSCRIPT_ARGS` — comma-joined leading Rscript options (`ir run --vanilla report.qmd`). Quarto's split has no escaping, so a comma-bearing option is rejected up front rather than mis-split.

Trailing arguments pass through to `quarto render` (`ir run report.qmd --to pdf`). The quarto executable is `IR_QUARTO` if set, else `quarto` on PATH, mirroring `IR_RSCRIPT`.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `ir run examples/hello.qmd` renders against the isolated library (needs R + rig + Quarto)
- [ ] A `.qmd` with no `ir:` key renders against the ambient library paths
- [ ] `.Rmd` routes to quarto; `.R` and extensionless scripts still run as scripts
- [ ] `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`

Builds on #18.

title: Add `ir tool run` for package executables
