title: Cache rig available data for `r-version` resolution
description:
## Summary
- Selects `r-version` from installed rig-managed R versions, and only consults available-version data when a matching installed R is missing.
- Avoids the hot-path `rig available --json` call for older `exclude-newer` dates by using an embedded available-version table, and falls back to `<cache>/rig/available.json` only for newer dates.
- Keeps `IR_RSCRIPT` as an explicit override and preserves the existing resolver flow for dependency materialisation.

## User-facing changes
- `ir run` now honors `r-version` / `--r-version` with rig-backed selection.
- `exclude-newer` no longer forces a network call when the date is covered by the embedded table.
- Error messages now point to a concrete `rig install` command when the requested R version is not installed.

## Internal changes
- Added a new `src/rig.rs` module to own rig integration and version selection.
- Embedded the known available R releases as typed data for the fast path, and added serde-backed parsing only for the cached `rig available --json` path.
- Updated CLI and resolver tests to cover embedded, cached, and missing-install cases.

title: Fix resolver stdin handling for `--with` dependencies
description:
## Summary
- Read resolver input from `file("stdin")` so `ir run --with ...` reaches the embedded R resolver through Rscript’s real stdin stream.
- Add a CLI regression that exercises the public `ir run` path against the real R resolver and verifies a `--with` package is materialized into the runtime library.
- This fixes the case where dependency specs were being skipped by the resolver, leaving the dynamic package library empty for user code.

## Notes
- The change is internal-only in the resolver path; the user-facing behavior is that `--with` packages now resolve and load as expected.

title: Add rig-backed R version resolution
description:
## Summary
- Switch frontmatter from `R` to `r-version` so scripts can select an installed R through `rig` instead of relying on the ambient `Rscript`.
- Add `exclude-newer` support with a simple ISO-date cutoff so version resolution ignores R releases after the requested date.
- Keep the existing package-resolution flow intact while making missing R versions fail with a direct `rig install ...` message.

## User-facing changes
- `r-version` now controls which R installation `ir` uses for both resolver and script execution.
- `exclude-newer` now limits the R versions considered by the resolver using a naive `YYYY-MM-DD` comparison.
- Error messages now tell users which `rig install` command to run when the requested R is not installed.

## Internal changes
- Parse rig JSON output for installed and available R versions, then map the selected R binary to its sibling `Rscript`.
- Update the R resolver helper and cache-key plumbing to use `exclude-newer`.
- Refresh examples, README text, and regression coverage for the new frontmatter keys and selection flow.

title: Add golden snapshots for CLI help output
description:
## Summary
- Add golden snapshot coverage for the public `ir` help output so API surface changes show up in diffs.
- Cover the top-level help plus `run`, `cache`, `cache clean`, and `cache dir` help output, including `-h` aliases and no-argument top-level help.
- Store the expected stdout under `tests/snapshots/` and compare it through a small integration test helper.

## Notes
- The change is test-only; there are no runtime code changes.

title: Use PATH Rscript when no R version is requested
description:
## Summary

This change makes R selection tests depend on controlled rig state while clarifying the default no-`r-version` behavior: `ir` should use `IR_RSCRIPT` when set, otherwise the `Rscript` found on `PATH`. Explicit `r-version` selection remains routed through rig.

Public-facing changes:
- Use `IR_RSCRIPT`, or the `Rscript` found on `PATH`, for runs and renders that do not request `r-version`.
- Stop using rig's default R install as an implicit fallback when `r-version` is absent.
- Pin Quarto renders to the same selected Rscript used for dependency resolution.
- Update README/config docs to reflect the default Rscript selection behavior.

Internal changes:
- Add rig-state test helpers that parse quiet `rig list --json` output and gate selection tests through `IR_TEST_R_VERSION`.
- Add PATH command resolution for `Rscript`, including Unix executable checks, symlink canonicalization, and supported Windows `PATHEXT` handling.
- Support Windows `Rscript.bat`/`.cmd` shims for default runs and render `QUARTO_R` pinning, while keeping unresolved batch wrappers out of resolution cache identity.
- Remove `rig::default_rscript()` and the unused `default` field from rig-installed R metadata.
- Add CLI coverage for PATH-vs-rig precedence, non-runnable PATH entries, Quarto pinning, Windows batch handling, warm cache reuse, and tool launcher generation.
- Pin Quarto test fixtures with `exclude-newer: 2026-06-01` so CI resolves the same package set across runners.

title: Enable Windows CI R bootstrap
description:
## Summary

Enable the Windows CI job to use the shared developer dependency bootstrap for rig and the non-default R needed by version-selection tests. This splits the Windows bootstrap work out of the larger CI polish branch so it can be reviewed on its own.

## User-facing changes

- Windows CI now provisions rig and R 4.4.3 through `scripts/install-dev-deps.ps1`, matching the Unix path used for version-selection coverage.
- The Windows dependency script supports `-Skip rust, python, quarto, r-release` so callers can keep tool setup owned by GitHub Actions while using the script for R tooling.
- The Unix and Windows developer dependency scripts no longer run `rig default release` unless callers explicitly pass `--set-rig-default` or `-SetRigDefault`.

## Internal changes

- Add a Windows `IR_RSCRIPT` pin before rig installation so CI keeps using the action-provided default R for normal runs.
- Teach `scripts/install-dev-deps.ps1` to install rig with Chocolatey on GitHub Actions, refresh common rig install paths, and require `winget` only when a winget-managed package is actually installed.
- Expand script/workflow tests for the Windows CI path, PowerShell skip-array binding, Chocolatey rig setup, lazy `winget` requirement, and opt-in-only rig default mutation.

title: Require all CI jobs before docs publish
description:
## Summary

Split the docs publishing gate out of #89 so it can land independently. The docs workflow was still carrying the old Windows CI exception and a manual publish bypass; this change makes docs publication depend on every CI job succeeding.

## User-facing changes

- Docs only publish after all CI jobs succeed, including Windows.
- Manual docs publishing no longer bypasses the CI job gate.

## Internal changes

- Grants `actions: read` so the docs workflow can inspect the triggering CI run's jobs.
- Removes the Windows-name filter from the CI job check and reports any failed CI job by name.
- Checks out the exact commit that triggered CI.
- Adds a regression test for the docs workflow gate.

title: Add MIT license file to packaged releases
description:
## Summary
- Include the new MIT `LICENSE` file in release archives so distributed binaries carry the license terms with them.
- Add a short license note to the README so users can find the license from the project landing page.
- This makes the packaged release more complete and reduces ambiguity for downstream users and redistributors.

## Changes
- Updated the release packaging workflow for macOS/Linux and Windows to copy `LICENSE` into the distributable bundle.
- Added a repository-level MIT `LICENSE` file.
- Added a README license section pointing to the license file.

## Notes
- No internal behavior changes beyond packaging and documentation.

title: Add PATH setup for installer and tool launchers
description:
## Summary
- Add automatic PATH setup for the `ir` installers and `ir tool install` so installed commands work from the common default locations without manual shell setup.
- Make platform behavior explicit: macOS updates `~/.zprofile` for the default `~/.local/bin`, Windows updates the user `Path`, and Linux continues to print a PATH hint when needed.
- Add `IR_NO_MODIFY_PATH` and `RAPP_NO_MODIFY_PATH` opt-outs and document the install-time behavior.

## User-facing changes
- `scripts/install.sh` writes a guarded macOS zsh profile snippet for the default Unix install directory and keeps the existing PATH hint when setup is skipped or not applicable.
- `scripts/install.ps1` normalizes and updates the current user `Path`, with duplicate detection, length checks, and warnings when the registry update cannot be applied.
- `ir tool install` sets up PATH for the default or environment-selected launcher directory after launchers are written successfully.
- Explicit custom `--bin-dir` installs remain custom locations and do not trigger the default macOS profile update.

## Internal changes
- Platform-specific PATH setup helpers are gated to the platforms that use them.
- The launcher PATH setup handles pre-existing default directories that are missing from PATH.
- macOS custom `--bin-dir` installs no longer canonicalize a missing default `~/.local/bin`.
- CLI coverage now includes installer PATH setup, macOS zprofile updates, custom bin-dir behavior, and failure ordering around launcher writes.

title: Handle Rapp package frontend entrypoints in tool run and install
description:
## Summary
- Treat a package-level `Rapp` file under `exec/` as the `Rapp` frontend so `tool run --from Rapp Rapp` and `tool install Rapp` work consistently
- Run the frontend without passing the app path to `Rapp::run()`, matching the package-specific launcher behavior
- Add an end-to-end CLI test that covers both running and installing the frontend for a sample Rapp app

title: Speed up CI with nextest and per-test isolation
description:
## Summary
- Switch CI from `cargo build` + `cargo test` to `cargo nextest run` so test execution is faster and more resilient.
- Add `taiki-e/install-action@nextest` to provision `nextest` in CI.
- Remove the shared end-to-end test lock and isolate fixtures, docs copies, and cache directories per test so tests can run safely in parallel.
- Add a regression check to ensure `tests/cli.rs` no longer relies on the global lock.

## Notes
- User-facing behavior is unchanged.
- The main internal change is making the integration test suite parallel-friendly.

title: Split CLI tests into focused domain suites
description:
## Summary
- Split the broad CLI test coverage into separate domain-specific suites so failures point to the relevant surface faster.
- This makes the test layout easier to navigate and maintain as `ir` grows, while keeping the public behavior covered by the same overall set of cases.

## Changes
- Reorganized CLI-related coverage across `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/render.rs`, `tests/rig_selection.rs`, `tests/run.rs`, `tests/scripts.rs`, and `tests/tool.rs`.
- Updated shared test helpers in `tests/support/mod.rs` to support the new structure.
- Kept the existing user-facing behavior coverage intact; the change is primarily about test organization and maintainability.
- No intended runtime behavior changes.

title: Add exclude-newer CLI and env overrides
description:
## Summary

Adds package snapshot-date overrides for source commands.
`ir run` and `ir render` now support `--exclude-newer <DATE>` and `IR_EXCLUDE_NEWER` in addition to frontmatter `exclude-newer`.

## Behavior

Snapshot date precedence for `ir run` and `ir render` is:

1. `--exclude-newer`
2. `IR_EXCLUDE_NEWER`
3. frontmatter `exclude-newer`
4. latest packages when none is set

Public-facing details:

- `--exclude-newer` wins over both env and frontmatter values.
- Non-empty CLI and env values are trimmed before resolution cache keying.
- Empty `--exclude-newer` and empty `IR_EXCLUDE_NEWER` override frontmatter `exclude-newer` and resolve latest packages.
- Future snapshot dates also resolve latest packages.
- `ir tool run` and `ir tool install` do not support snapshot overrides and do not inherit ambient `IR_EXCLUDE_NEWER`.

## Internal Changes

- Apply source-command snapshot overrides to `RuntimeSpec` before R version selection, cache keying, and dependency resolution.
- Normalize blank and future snapshot override values to no snapshot date before resolution.
- Remove ambient `IR_EXCLUDE_NEWER` from resolver subprocesses, then pass only the normalized `RuntimeSpec` value for supported commands.
- Update CLI help snapshots and user docs for `--exclude-newer`, `IR_EXCLUDE_NEWER`, and precedence.

## Testing

- `cargo test exclude_newer`
- `cargo test help_outputs_match_snapshots`

title: Serialize dependency resolution per shared cache
description:
## Summary

Serialize dependency resolution for runs that share the same `ir` cache, so concurrent invocations do not launch overlapping `resolve.R` processes against shared R and renv cache state.

The lock is intentionally cache-wide: unrelated dependency sets also wait for the active resolver before starting their own resolution.

## Public-facing changes

- Concurrent runs sharing `IR_CACHE_DIR` now wait for active dependency resolution to finish.
- Warm resolution markers still skip the resolver.
- A waiting process rechecks the marker after acquiring the lock, so same-dependency concurrent runs can reuse work completed by the first process.

## Internal changes

- Adds a Rust-owned file lock at `locks/resolver.lock` before launching `resolve.R`.
- Rechecks the resolution cache after acquiring the lock.
- Leaves `resolve.R` lock-free, with no R-side locking dependency.
- Adds CLI regression coverage for same-dependency resolver dedupe and different-dependency resolver serialization.

title: Use requested R version in install hints
description:
## Summary

Exact R version requirements already mean the requested version must be installed. This change keeps the missing-version error aligned with that request instead of echoing the comparison operator or a resolved patch candidate.

## User-facing changes

- `--r-version "== 4.4"` now reports `R 4.4 is required` and suggests `rig install 4.4`.
- The same requested-version wording is used when `exclude-newer` is also set.

## Internal changes

- Reuses the parsed install hint when formatting missing R errors.
- Updates public CLI regression coverage for exact major, exact minor, and exact minor plus `exclude-newer`.

title: Fix rig tooling runtime selection
description:
## Summary

Fix two resolver startup hazards that can surface on arm macOS when R installs and resolver tooling libraries overlap across runtimes.

## User-facing changes

- R selection through rig now keeps choosing the highest matching version, but same-version ties prefer rig's default install.
- On arm macOS, same-version ties without a rig default prefer an install whose rig name or path contains `-arm64`.
- Resolver startup no longer reuses user-library tooling packages built for a different R minor runtime or platform.
- Resolver startup repairs an unloadable private `pak` install before using it.

## Internal changes

- Deserializes rig's `default` and `path` metadata for deterministic same-version tie-breaking.
- Verifies private `pak` can load from the private tooling library before treating it as available.
- Removes an unloadable private `pak` directory before bootstrapping a replacement.
- Adds CLI regression coverage for rig same-version selection and resolver tooling compatibility.

## Notes

This branch intentionally excludes Python metadata changes.

title: Add a scoped test cleanup helper for temporary paths
description:
## Summary
- Introduce a scoped cleanup helper for test temp paths so fixtures and integration tests can manage scratch state with less repeated teardown code.
- Reduce cleanup boilerplate across resolver, rig selection, run, render, and tool tests to make the test suite easier to maintain and less error-prone.
- Keep the change internal to the test support layer; there are no user-facing CLI changes.

## Notes
- Updates are concentrated in `tests/support/` with corresponding call site changes in the affected test files.
- The new helper centralizes temporary-path lifecycle handling and makes cleanup behavior explicit at the point of use.

title: Use Linux PPM binary repositories for snapshot resolution
description:
## Summary
- Switch default and snapshot CRAN resolution to Posit Package Manager binary URLs on Linux distributions that expose a known distro codename.
- Keep non-Linux behavior unchanged while still preferring PPM latest for default repository resolution.
- Update the CI cache warmup path to use `--snapshot` instead of raw `--repos` URLs so the script can derive the correct PPM endpoint itself.
- Refresh the docs to explain that `ir` now resolves public PPM repositories through distro-specific binary URLs on supported Linux hosts.

## Changes
- Added Linux distro detection in the R resolver and cache warmup script, including support for Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL-family, CentOS, and openSUSE Leap.
- Centralized PPM URL construction so both tooling installs and user package resolution use the same snapshot-to-URL mapping.
- Extended test coverage to verify default, latest, and snapshot repository selection paths on Linux.
- Updated CI workflow expectations to match the new snapshot-driven repository selection.

title: Support Python metadata in R scripts
description:
## Summary

Add Python environment metadata support to regular `ir run` R scripts, and route script and Quarto Python environment resolution through the shared resolver path. This lets self-describing R scripts declare R and Python requirements together while keeping resolver locking, cache reuse, and snapshot behavior consistent.

## User-facing changes

- `ir run` now reads `python-packages`, `python-version`, and `python-exclude-newer` from `#|` script frontmatter.
- `ir run` and `ir render` now accept `--python-exclude-newer` to use a different Python package snapshot date from R package resolution.
- When Python metadata is present, `exclude-newer` is used for Python resolution by default unless `python-exclude-newer` is set.
- Empty or `null` `python-exclude-newer` resolves latest Python packages while leaving R `exclude-newer` behavior unchanged.
- Resolved Python environments are activated for the launched process: `PATH`/`VIRTUAL_ENV` are set, `PYTHONHOME` is cleared, and `RETICULATE_PYTHON` is set.
- Python package executables installed in the resolved environment are available to R scripts through subprocess calls.
- Script, Quarto, cache, config, help snapshot, and README docs now describe the combined R/Python metadata behavior.

## Internal changes

- Python environment requests use separate cache markers that record the resolved Python executable path and refresh when the path is missing.
- Python cache keys include declared packages, render-only `jupyter` injection, `python-version`, and normalized Python snapshot selection.
- Latest Python environment cache entries use the same max-age policy as latest R package resolution, while snapshot cache entries remain immutable.
- Python and R resolution now share the embedded `resolve.R` driver and resolver lock; the standalone Python resolver driver was removed.
- Runtime resolution checks R and Python cache entries before and after the resolver lock, then resolves only the missing pieces in one resolver invocation when needed.
- Python resolver env vars are cleared before spawning `resolve.R` so stale ambient `IR_PYTHON_*` values cannot trigger accidental Python resolution.
- Empty Python package requests now write an empty package file instead of a blank package entry.
- Regression coverage was added for script Python metadata, environment activation, clearing `PYTHONHOME`, Python-specific `exclude-newer`, empty Python package requests, separate Python cache refresh, combined R/Python version pins, Quarto render behavior, resolver env cleanup, and concurrent resolver locking.

title: Remove prompt prefixes from README commands
description:
## Summary

Update the README examples so commands can be copied and pasted directly without carrying shell prompt characters into the terminal.

## User-facing changes

- Remove `$` and `>` prompt prefixes from README command blocks, including the Unix and PowerShell install snippets.
- Use `sh` and `powershell` fences for command examples so the shell context is still clear without embedding prompts.

## Internal changes

- Add a regression test for the README install section to keep prompt-prefixed command lines out of copyable install instructions.
- Normalize CRLF line endings in that test so it passes on Windows checkouts.

title: Retry resolver after tooling restarts and crashes
description:
## Summary

This makes dependency resolution more resilient when resolver tooling needs to be installed, upgraded, or isolated from a problematic ambient R library.

## Public-facing changes

- No new CLI flags or metadata fields.
- `ir run` and `ir render` can retry dependency resolution after resolver tooling requests a clean restart.
- Resolver process crashes are retried once in safe tooling mode, which excludes user/site libraries and startup files before failing.
- Normal resolver failures still fail without retrying.

## Internal-only changes

- Keys the private tooling cache by R version, platform, package refs, and minimum version requirements.
- Reworks tooling availability checks around `requireNamespace()` instead of metadata pruning user libraries on the fast path.
- Adds resolver restart signaling through a restart file and status code.
- Adds CLI integration coverage for ambient tooling, real `pak` installs, safe-mode crash retry, restart after closed stdin, Python render retry, and cache marker timing.

title: Install latest rig release in CI bootstrap
description:
## Summary

This makes CI and developer bootstrap more robust when package-manager channels lag a newly published rig release. macOS now installs rig from the latest upstream `.pkg`, and Windows GitHub Actions installs rig from the latest upstream `.exe`.

## User-facing changes

- macOS setup resolves the latest rig release at runtime and installs the matching upstream package for the current architecture.
- Windows local setup keeps using `winget`, while Windows GitHub Actions resolves and installs the latest upstream rig installer.
- `--dry-run` stays deterministic and does not resolve the latest release over the network.

## Internal changes

- Added dependency-light POSIX latest-release resolution through GitHub's release redirect.
- Added PowerShell release API lookup, architecture-specific asset selection, and `Start-Process -Wait -PassThru` installer execution.
- Updated script tests to reject pinned rig versions and obsolete Homebrew/Chocolatey rig install paths.

title: Add ir quickstart and expand rx help
description:
## Summary

Adds `ir quickstart` as a concise, agent-facing guide for producing portable, self-describing R scripts and Quarto documents.

The guidance explains the intended artifact style: put runtime metadata in frontmatter, let `ir` resolve dependencies into ephemeral cached environments, and keep the script or document body as plain R or Quarto code. It also gives agents a brief mental model for package tools: `rx` and `ir tool run` execute package-provided frontends in isolated resolved tool environments. Because this guidance is agent-facing, the website keeps it low-prominence in the Reference page instead of adding a dedicated navigation page.

For `rx`, this avoids adding a separate quickstart command because bare arguments already name package executables. Instead, `rx --help` now carries the focused tool-executable guidance.

## User Facing Changes

- Adds `ir quickstart`, listed after `tool` in the root help output.
- Documents dependency resolution through ephemeral cached environments, ambient user-library behavior with and without `isolated: true`, Python dependency metadata, `exclude-newer`, rig/R requirements, Quarto requirements, argument boundaries, and package tool usage.
- Expands `rx --help` with the package-executable mental model, isolation behavior, examples, and workflow guidance.
- Keeps `quickstart` available as a normal `rx` package/executable shorthand rather than reserving `rx quickstart` or `rx --quickstart`.
- Keeps website documentation low-prominence by placing `ir quickstart` near the bottom of the Reference page.

## Internal Changes

- Adds a `quickstart` module and routes the new `ir` subcommand through the existing CLI dispatch.
- Stores the `ir quickstart` text in a source file and snapshots the command output.
- Leaves the `rx` shim as a delegator to `ir tool rx`; the extra guidance lives in the hidden `tool rx` help used by `rx --help`.
- Extends CLI snapshot coverage for `ir quickstart`, `ir quickstart --help`, root help, and expanded `rx --help`.
- Adds tests covering that `rx --quickstart` is not a supported special mode and that `rx quickstart --help` can still run a package executable named `quickstart`.
- Adds render coverage to ensure quickstart is not present in the website nav/home/tools pages and remains near the bottom of Reference.
- Makes the reference-page CLI helper choose and normalize `ir.exe` on Windows when `IR_BIN` is not set. The quickstart docs test renders the reference page on non-Windows platforms and checks the same low-prominence source placement directly on Windows.

## Notes

No resolver, runtime execution, or dependency bootstrap behavior changes.

title: Update repository links for r-lib move
description:
## Summary

The repository moved from `t-kalinowski/ir` to `r-lib/ir`, so public install and documentation links now need to resolve from the new owner.

## User-facing changes

- README and install documentation commands now use `raw.githubusercontent.com/r-lib/ir`.
- Documentation links now point to `https://r-lib.github.io/ir/`.
- Unix and Windows installers now download releases from `r-lib/ir`.

## Internal changes

- Added a regression test for stale public `t-kalinowski/ir` links in docs and installers.

title: Inject reticulate for knitr Python chunks
description:
## Summary

Knitr-backed Quarto documents with Python chunks can benefit from `reticulate` for Python execution, but resolving the full Quarto project with `quarto inspect` would make render setup slower. This change uses local document/frontmatter scanning to decide when `ir render` should add `reticulate` to the R dependency seed, while keeping Jupyter documents on the Python environment path.

## User-facing changes

- `ir render` now adds `reticulate` for `.Rmd` files and knitr-backed `.qmd` files with local Python chunks when the resolved R package set does not already provide it.
- `.qmd` engine detection covers top-level `engine: knitr` / `engine: jupyter`, `execute.engine`, and format-scoped execute engines.
- The detector recognizes backtick and tilde executable fences, YAML `...` frontmatter terminators, longer valid closing fences, and ignores four-space-indented literal fence examples.
- Jupyter renders remain reticulate-free; declaring `ir.python-packages` or `ir.python-version` asks `ir render` to create the Python environment and include `jupyter`.

## Internal changes

- Added a lightweight local Quarto/R Markdown chunk scanner instead of calling `quarto inspect`.
- Added `IR_QUARTO_RETICULATE` as a resolver signal and cache-key input.
- Added public CLI regression coverage for knitr/Jupyter reticulate selection and chunk/frontmatter edge cases.
- Updated Quarto docs and quickstart wording to distinguish reticulate injection from Jupyter environment injection.

title: Remove rscript frontmatter metadata
description:
## Summary

Remove support for `rscript` in script and Quarto frontmatter because executable paths or commands are machine-specific. Source metadata should use `r-version`; operators can still override local R selection with `--rscript` or `IR_RSCRIPT`.

Fixes #122.

## User-facing changes

- `rscript:` in script frontmatter now fails with a clear error pointing to `--rscript` or `IR_RSCRIPT`.
- `ir.rscript:` in Quarto metadata is rejected with the same guidance.
- README, docs, and quickstart text describe Rscript selection as a CLI or environment override.

## Internal changes

- `RuntimeSpec` no longer stores frontmatter Rscript selection.
- Frontmatter R selection now only resolves `r-version`.
- Public CLI regression tests cover script and Quarto rejection while preserving existing `--rscript` and `IR_RSCRIPT` override behavior.

title: Support package bin tools with durable installs
description:
## Summary

Adds package tool discovery for installed R package `bin/` directories, including architecture-specific `bin/<arch>/` directories, so tools produced by R package install hooks can be run through `rx` and installed through `ir tool install`.

Installed tools now use a durable tool store configured by `IR_TOOL_STORE_DIR`, so their package libraries survive `ir cache clean`.

Closes https://github.com/t-kalinowski/ir/issues/119.

## User-facing changes

- `rx` and `ir tool run` can resolve package executables from `bin/` and `bin/<arch>/` in addition to `exec/`.
- `ir tool install` writes launchers for package `bin/` executables backed by durable installed-tool libraries.
- Package `bin/` entries are treated as opaque executables with exact file-name command names.
- Architecture-specific `bin/<arch>/` tools use the selected R architecture for discovery, runtime `PATH`, and installed launchers.
- `ir cache clean` removes run/render cache state but does not remove installed tool libraries under `IR_TOOL_STORE_DIR`.
- Package tool help and docs now describe direct executable scripts and binaries from `exec/`, `bin/`, and `bin/<arch>/`.

## Internal changes

- Centralizes package executable directory discovery across `exec/`, `bin/`, and architecture-specific `bin/` subdirectories.
- Adds runtime `PATH` prefixing for resolved package `bin/` directories so launched tools can find sibling package executables.
- Adds resolver support for an alternate installed-tool library root while keeping resolution markers in `IR_CACHE_DIR`.
- Includes Rscript architecture args and the library root in resolution cache keys.
- Adds Windows wrapper and target-collision handling for installed `bin/` executables.
- Adds an R package fixture with a Cargo CLI project under `tools/irrustbin` and install-time `bin/`/`bin/<arch>/` entries.
- Adds public CLI regression coverage for `ir tool run`, `rx`, `ir tool install`, installed launchers, durable tool storage, and architecture-specific `bin/` tools.
- Passes GitHub authentication headers to the Windows rig release lookup in CI/dev dependency setup.

title: Add rig install guidance to installers
description:
## Summary
- Print platform-specific `rig` installation guidance when it is missing during `ir` install
- Update the README and installer docs to tell users the installers will surface `rig` setup help
- Add script coverage to keep the public installer messaging aligned across shells

## Notes
- The guidance covers macOS, Linux, and Windows with direct install commands or reference links
- Internal changes are limited to installer script messaging and a small regression test

title: Add a daily GitHub Actions cache for the R user library
description:
## Summary
- Cache the R user library in CI under a UTC day bucket so repeated runs within the same day reuse downloads while still forcing a fresh cache daily.
- Move the cached directory to `runner.temp` and seed it explicitly before dependency installation.
- Pass the daily cache date through `setup-r-dependencies` so the package cache version stays aligned with the new bucketed cache.
- Update workflow coverage to assert the new cache location, cache key, and the absence of restore keys.
- This reduces CI time and keeps the cache behavior predictable without changing the public CLI surface.
- Internal-only change: workflow and test updates only.
- No user-facing runtime behavior changes.

title: Clean up pak resolver subprocess tempdirs
description:
## Summary

Fixes resolver-owned pak subprocess cleanup so dependency resolution does not leave pak/pkgcache metadata files behind in stale R temp directories. The change keeps pak using its normal cache paths while making child R tempdirs live under the resolver's tempdir and closing pak's callr session before the resolver exits.

## User-facing changes

- Reduces accumulation of stale `Rtmp*` directories from resolver pak calls.
- Prevents repeated `Rtmp*/file*/_metadata/pkgs-*.rds` files from surviving normal resolver completion.
- Does not add a second persistent package metadata cache.

## Internal changes

- Adds shared resolver helpers to set child `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, and `TEMP` to the current resolver `tempdir()`.
- Closes pak's cached remote session on dependency and Python resolver exit.
- Avoids computing primary-package cache markers when the caller does not request primary package metadata.
- Adds a CLI regression test covering child tempdir propagation and pak remote cleanup.

title: Support Python frontmatter for Quarto renders
description:
## Public changes

Adds `ir.python-packages` and `ir.python-version` support for Quarto documents. `ir render` now resolves a Python environment through reticulate/uv, injects `jupyter`, and passes the resolved executable to Quarto with `QUARTO_PYTHON` and `RETICULATE_PYTHON`.

Documents can declare R dependencies with `ir.packages` and Python dependencies with `ir.python-packages`. `ir.exclude-newer` is shared across both resolvers where applicable, and `ir.r-version` cannot be combined with `ir.python-version`.

## Internal changes

Splits resolver tooling into shared embedded driver code used by both R package resolution and Python environment resolution. Cached driver files are now content-hashed so stale embedded drivers are not reused after changes.

Adds a separate Python resolver path, shares resolver locking for Python tooling setup, and moves resolver tooling tests out of the broader run test file.

title: Resolve version-selection test R dynamically
description:
## Summary

This changes local and CI setup to install rig's `oldrel/2` for version-selection coverage instead of pinning the secondary test R to `4.4.3`.

The goal is to keep the test matrix useful as R releases advance: setup now asks rig which concrete R release `oldrel/2` means, exports that version plus its matching snapshot date, and uses the matching `Rscript` when warming the non-default cache.

## User-facing changes

- `scripts/install-dev-deps.sh` and `scripts/install-dev-deps.ps1` now provision `oldrel/2` for the non-default test R.
- Setup output now reports `IR_TEST_R_VERSION`, `IR_TEST_R_EXCLUDE_NEWER`, and `IR_TEST_RSCRIPT`.
- Added `--skip test-r` / `-Skip test-r` for callers that do not want the secondary test R installed.
- Setup no longer offers or runs the rig default mutation option.
- README setup docs now describe the dynamic `oldrel/2` install instead of hard-coded R `4.4.3`.

## Internal changes

- Added a shared `scripts/resolve-test-r.py` helper that delegates `oldrel/2` resolution to rig, maps the resolved version to the installed rig name, and reads release metadata from that R.
- CI now warms the non-default R cache using `IR_TEST_RSCRIPT` and the resolved `IR_TEST_R_EXCLUDE_NEWER` snapshot.
- `scripts/warm-renv-cache.R` now respects `R_LIBS_USER` so the non-default cache warm can target an isolated library.
- Version-selection fixtures are rewritten at test time to use the resolved R version and snapshot date.
- Script and rig-selection coverage was updated around dynamic test-R metadata, cache warming, and preserving minor-line `exclude-newer` behavior.

title: Select R from exclude-newer date
description:
## Summary

- Split the `exclude-newer` runtime-selection behavior out of #89 so it can be reviewed independently.
- When `exclude-newer` is set without `r-version`, `ir` now chooses the newest installed stable R version released on or before that date.
- Keep explicit `r-version` authoritative when both fields are present.

## User-facing changes

- `exclude-newer` now pins both CRAN resolution and default R selection by date.
- README and docs describe that rig is required for `exclude-newer` and that `IR_RSCRIPT` is ignored for date-selected runs.
- The Scripts docs now spell out how `r-version` and `exclude-newer` interact across installed-R scenarios.

## Internal changes

- Preserve the embedded build-time R release table as the fast path for dated R selection and install hints, avoiding `rig available` calls when embedded data already answers a covered date.
- Expand the embedded table to patch releases, so historical dates such as `2024-01-15` can select installed R 4.3.2.
- Select from installed rig versions first, instead of requiring the globally newest release for the date to be installed.
- Check installed releases unknown to the embedded table before returning embedded selections or install hints.
- Query rig with `available --all --json` when the embedded table and cached rig data cannot answer a dated installed-release lookup or install recommendation.
- Cache `rig available --all --json` under `IR_CACHE_DIR/rig/available.json` with the latest observed stable release date and a `checked_at` Unix timestamp.
- Use a 24-hour TTL for the rig availability cache, so future `exclude-newer` requests reuse a fresh cache instead of repeatedly calling `rig available`.
- Filter unrequested symbolic rig availability names such as `release`, `oldrel`, `next`, and `devel` out of broad `r-version` matches and date-based install hints.
- Filter installed prerelease aliases such as `next` and `devel` out of broad `r-version` matches unless the user explicitly requests that rig name.
- Skip incomplete `rig list --json` records when selecting dated R versions.
- Use real rig in R-selection regression tests, including future-cutoff cache reuse, symbolic availability install hints, symbolic prerelease install selection, and explicit `r-version` precedence.

title: Select installed R for exclude-newer runs
description:
## Summary
- Extend `exclude-newer` to do more than pin CRAN resolution: when `r-version` is omitted, `ir` now selects the newest installed R released on or before the cutoff date.
- This keeps package resolution and R version selection aligned to the same date-based reproducibility boundary.

## Changes
- Update runtime selection so `exclude-newer` can resolve an Rscript path without an explicit `r-version`.
- Expand the embedded and cached `rig available` handling so `ir` can compare installed R versions against release dates.
- Ignore `IR_RSCRIPT` whenever `exclude-newer` is active, matching the new `rig`-based selection path.
- Add coverage for date-based R selection with an end-to-end CLI test.
- Refresh README and config docs to describe the new behavior and requirements.

title: Make R selection first-class and infer R minor from exclude-newer
description:
## Summary

This makes R selection consistent across `ir` commands and tightens date-based reproducibility.

Previously, `IR_RSCRIPT` behaved like a special escape hatch while `r-version` could be supplied through frontmatter or CLI. This PR makes `rscript` and `r-version` first-class R selectors with a shared precedence model: CLI, then environment, then frontmatter. It also lets date-only `exclude-newer` imply the latest R minor version available on that date when no explicit R selector is provided.

## User-facing changes

- Adds `--rscript <RSCRIPT>` to `ir run`, `ir render`, `ir tool run`, `rx`, and `ir tool install`.
- Adds frontmatter `rscript`.
- Adds `IR_R_VERSION` as the environment form of `r-version`.
- Keeps `IR_RSCRIPT`, now as the environment form of `rscript`.
- Resolves R selection in this order:
  - CLI `--rscript` / `--r-version`
  - environment `IR_RSCRIPT` / `IR_R_VERSION`
  - frontmatter `rscript` / `r-version`
  - R minor implied by date-only `exclude-newer`
  - default `Rscript` on `PATH`
- Treats `rscript` and `r-version` as mutually exclusive within the same layer, while allowing higher-precedence layers to override lower ones.
- Uses date-only `exclude-newer` to select the latest R major.minor available on that date, then requires a matching installed R. If that minor is missing, the error gives a minor install hint such as `rig install 4.4`.
- For snapshot dates after the embedded R metadata fetch date, uses a refreshed cached R minor release list so older `ir` binaries do not silently select a stale minor.
- Updates Quarto wording around the selected R executable and continues setting `QUARTO_R`.
- Preserves selected R in generated tool launchers and recovery commands, including `--rscript`, env-selected R, and Windows command quoting.

## Internal changes

- Refactors R selection into a single runtime path shared by run, render, and tool commands.
- Replaces embedded available-release metadata with embedded first-release dates per R minor plus an embedded metadata fetch date.
- Replaces the old full available-release cache with a minor-release cache used only when date-only `exclude-newer` is newer than the embedded metadata.
- Updates CLI help snapshots and docs to describe the new selector model.
- Updates CI cache warming to prewarm reticulate from GitHub and use explicit default CRAN behavior for non-tooling package cache warming.

title: Fail fast when requested R version is not installed
description:
## Summary

When an explicit R version is requested and no installed R matches, fail directly from the installed R list instead of querying `rig available --json`.

This keeps the missing-version path simpler and avoids an unnecessary external lookup that can obscure the actual error. It also makes short exact-version requests behave as series requests: `== 4` means `4.*.*`, and `== 4.4` means `4.4.*`, selecting the latest installed matching version rather than treating omitted components as `0`.

## User-facing changes

- `ir run --r-version <version>` now reports a missing installed R directly when no installed version matches.
- `--r-version 4` and `--r-version "== 4"` select an installed `4.x`, choosing the latest matching installed version.
- `--r-version "== 4.4"` selects an installed `4.4.x`, choosing the latest matching patch when multiple patches are installed.
- Short series specs still succeed with an older matching installed version when that is the only matching installed R.
- If no installed matching series exists, the error remains direct and does not query `rig available --json`.
- `exclude-newer` behavior is unchanged and still uses R availability metadata where needed.

## Internal changes

- Added helper setup for fake installed R binaries in `rig_selection` tests.
- Added named CLI tests for major-series and minor-series selection with:
  - multiple installed matching versions
  - only one installed matching version
  - installed versions from other series only
- Added CLI regression coverage proving the missing explicit version path does not call `rig available --json`.
- Added a small helper for deriving `rig install` hints from bare and `==` R version requirements.

title: Generate embedded R availability table
description:
## Summary

This replaces the hand-written embedded R availability table with one generated from checked-in r-hub R release metadata.

This PR is staging infrastructure for follow-up R selection work. It does not add a CLI flag, frontmatter field, or intended user-facing behavior change. In particular, it does not make `exclude-newer` imply an `r-version`; that remains for the follow-up `set-rversion-from-excludenewer` work.

Internal changes:
- Add checked-in r-hub R release metadata plus a refresh script.
- Parse that JSON during the Cargo build.
- Generate the embedded `AvailableCandidate` list from parsed release metadata instead of hand-writing it in `rig_releases.rs`.
- Add a reusable release metadata parser for future runtime metadata work.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`

title: Split rig selection and release handling
description:
## Summary
- Split rig-related responsibility into smaller modules for selection, client access, and release handling.
- Keep the public CLI behavior the same while making the rig path easier to follow and maintain.
- Move shared CLI test support into `tests/support` so path lookup logic is reused instead of duplicated.

## Notes
- User-facing behavior is unchanged.
- The main effect is internal structure and test support cleanup.

title: Stabilize the Windows CI test job
description:
Two changes toward a meaningful Windows CI job, both in the dependency-fixture tests.

## Reframe the availability probe

`ci_dependencies_are_available` loaded all 16 fixture packages into a single R session with `requireNamespace`. On windows-latest that co-loads their native DLLs and faults the session with `0xC0000005`.

Investigation (debug branch, now removed) showed each package loads cleanly on its own — including `secretbase`, so it is not an ABI mismatch — and only the all-at-once load crashes. No `ir` workflow co-loads these packages: `ir` resolves a single document's dependencies into an isolated library and loads only those. The probe invented an unrealistic 16-way co-load and failed on an artifact of its own construction. (Installing dev `sessioninfo` did not help, and the probe never calls `platform_info()`, so #46's sessioninfo theory does not apply here.)

Switched to `find.package(p, quiet = TRUE)`, which confirms each package is installed without `dlopen` — all this check needs.

## Skip the still-broken e2e tests on Windows

Four real-toolchain fixture tests fail only on the runner and each needs its own root-cause:

- `run_inline_expression_resolves_with_dependencies` — `0xC0000005` native co-load crash
- `run_script_fixture_resolves_packages_and_isolates_user_library` — same resolution path
- `tool_install_installs_real_package_entrypoint` — depends on that resolution
- `run_reticulate_fixture_imports_python_module` — reticulate cannot find the runner Python

Marked `#[cfg_attr(windows, ignore = "...#46")]` so they still run on Linux and macOS while the Windows job keeps exercising snapshots, arg parsing, cache behaviour, and (once #52 lands) the cross-drive render — instead of staying permanently red.

Depends on #52 for a fully green Windows job (the cross-drive `--output-dir` render is fixed there, not here).

Related to #46

description:
## Summary

- Split the `exclude-newer` runtime-selection behavior out of #89 so it can be reviewed independently.
- When `exclude-newer` is set without `r-version`, `ir` now chooses the newest installed stable R version released on or before that date.
- Keep explicit `r-version` authoritative when both fields are present.

## User-facing changes

- `exclude-newer` now pins both CRAN resolution and default R selection by date.
- README and docs describe that rig is required for `exclude-newer` and that `IR_RSCRIPT` is ignored for date-selected runs.

## Internal changes

- Preserve the embedded build-time R release table as the common path for dated R selection.
- Expand the embedded table to patch releases, so historical dates such as `2024-01-15` can select installed R 4.3.2.
- Select from installed rig versions first, instead of requiring the globally newest release for the date to be installed.
- Check installed releases unknown to the embedded table before returning an embedded-known selection, including historical installs older than the embedded table.
- Query rig with `available --all --json` when the embedded table cannot answer a dated installed-release lookup.
- Cache `rig available --all --json` publication dates under `IR_CACHE_DIR/rig/available.json` using the latest observed release date as cache coverage, not the requested cutoff.
- Accept only the current object-shaped rig availability cache; array-shaped development caches are rejected instead of migrated.
- Skip incomplete `rig list --json` records when selecting dated R versions.
- Add CLI regression coverage for installed fallback, historical patch releases, unknown historical and future installed releases, cached release-date reuse, stale/future-cutoff cache refreshes, stale cache shape rejection, broken rig entries, and explicit `r-version` precedence.

title: Update docs and tool help for package executable behavior
description:
## Summary
- Clarify the README and Quarto docs to use consistent project/runtime terminology and tighten the `rmarkdown` override guidance.
- Update tool documentation and CLI help to describe tools as supported executables in a package `exec/` directory, including the distinction between `Rscript`/`Rapp` entries and direct executable scripts.
- Add platform-specific note for direct executables on Unix and Windows so users know which files are valid launch targets.
- Keep the help snapshot aligned with the revised public wording.

## Notes

- Internal code changes are limited to the CLI help text surfaced by `ir tool --help`.

title: Add cross-platform dev dependency bootstrap scripts
description:
## Summary
- Add Unix and Windows setup scripts to install the build and test prerequisites for `ir` on a fresh machine.
- Make the bootstrap path explicit so contributors can install Rust, Python, rig, Quarto, and the extra R 4.4.3 used by version-selection tests without manually piecing together platform-specific steps.
- Update CI to reuse the Unix bootstrap script for rig and the non-default R setup, reducing duplicated workflow logic and keeping local setup closer to CI.
- Document the new development setup flow in `README.md`, including dry-run support for inspecting the planned installs.
- Add tests that lock in the script plans and the CI workflow expectations.
- Internal changes are limited to setup/bootstrap paths; public CLI behavior is unchanged.

title: Support direct executable package tools in ir
description:
## Summary
- Add support for package `exec/` entries that are ordinary executable scripts, while preserving existing Rscript, Rapp, and Rapp frontend dispatch behavior.
- Generate installed launchers that run direct scripts directly and keep the resolved tool runtime environment, including PATH setup for package exec directories.
- Update package tool docs to describe direct executable scripts as supported package tools.

## Why
Some packages ship useful command-line tools as shell, Python, or platform script entrypoints rather than Rscript/Rapp launchers. These should be runnable through `rx` / `ir tool run` and installable with `ir tool install`.

## User-facing changes
- `rx` and `ir tool run` can run supported direct executable scripts from package `exec/`.
- `ir tool install` can install persistent launchers for those direct scripts.
- Direct scripts reject forwarded Rscript options, since those options only apply to Rscript/Rapp executables.

## Internal changes
- Add a `Direct` package launcher kind and platform-specific direct script detection.
- Keep Rapp's package frontend special case from being discovered twice.
- Add public CLI coverage for running and installing shell/Python direct package scripts.

title: Fix inline-expression arg forwarding in `ir run`
description:
## Summary
- Fix `ir run -e ...` so option-like arguments after the inline expression are treated as user program arguments instead of being consumed as Rscript options.
- This keeps inline-expression runs aligned with the documented boundary between `ir` flags and user arguments.
- Add a regression test that exercises `commandArgs(TRUE)` with a trailing `--script-flag` argument.

## Internal Changes
- Tighten `parse_run_args` in `src/cli.rs` so parsing stops at the first non-expression argument once `-e`/`--expr` has been seen.
- Update the parser comment to describe the inline-expression boundary more clearly.
- Add a public CLI integration test covering the forwarding behavior.

title: Move Quarto rendering to ir render
description:
## Summary

Moves Quarto rendering out of `ir run` and into a dedicated `ir render` subcommand, closing #61 and leaving `ir run` focused on Rscript execution.

## User-facing changes

- Adds `ir render <source>` for `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, and Quarto-formatted R scripts.
- Reports a direct error when `ir run` receives a Quarto document, pointing users to `ir render <source>`.
- Updates README, docs, CLI reference output, and help snapshots to use `ir render`.

## Internal changes

- Splits run and render sources so Quarto dispatch is command-driven instead of inferred by `ir run`.
- Adds a render runtime path that still uses the existing resolver and `rmarkdown` injection behavior.
- Adds regression coverage for the new render subcommand, migrated Quarto document cases, and Quarto R script rendering.

title: Split Rust source into focused modules
description:
## Summary

This refactors the Rust CLI source layout so `main.rs` is no longer responsible for CLI parsing, script metadata parsing, runtime resolution, cache commands, and package tool execution in one large file.

## User-facing changes

- No intended CLI behavior changes.
- Existing run, cache, and tool commands keep the same public command shape.

## Internal changes

- Keeps `main.rs` as a small entrypoint and command router.
- Moves clap command setup and argument parsing into `src/cli.rs`.
- Moves script source and frontmatter parsing into `src/script.rs`.
- Moves R runtime selection, dependency resolution, and execution helpers into `src/runtime.rs`.
- Moves package executable run/install handling into `src/tool.rs`.
- Moves cache subcommand handling into `src/cache.rs`.
- Updates `rig.rs` to call the moved cache directory helper through `runtime`.

title: Switch latest cache markers to timestamps
description:
## Summary

Switch latest resolution cache markers from UTC dates to Unix timestamps so cache freshness is measured as elapsed seconds instead of calendar-day boundaries. This keeps the latest cache key stable while making refresh behavior a predictable 24-hour window.

## User-facing changes

- Latest resolution cache entries now refresh after `IR_LATEST_RESOLUTION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`, defaulting to 86400 seconds.
- Cache and configuration docs describe the timestamp marker and new environment variable.
- Quarto and tool docs use the newer package-oriented wording.

## Internal changes

- Rust cache reads now parse `latest: <unix timestamp>` and compare marker age directly.
- The embedded R resolver fallback uses the same timestamp marker and max-age check.
- The `time` crate and its transitive lockfile entries are removed.
- CLI regression coverage checks fresh timestamp reuse, configurable max age, and stale marker refresh.

title: Sync website docs with bootstrapped tooling and rmarkdown injection
description:
The resolver-tooling bootstrap and the auto-injected `rmarkdown` for Quarto renders (#45) reached `README.md`, but the website pages were not fully synced.

- The Config page listed `pak`/`renv`/`secretbase` as a user prerequisite. `ir` installs them on first use, so this was incorrect.
- The Quarto page never documented the auto-injected `rmarkdown` or its pin advisory.
- The README now links to the published docs site (#51).

Related to #45, #51

title: Move docs publishing to its own workflow
description:
The docs job gated on `needs: [test, lint]`, so any failing test matrix leg blocked publishing. The Windows test leg is expected to fail until the `\\?\` path bug in `ir run` is fixed (#32), which has kept the website from updating on every push to `main`.

Publishing now lives in `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, triggered on CI completion. Rather than gating on the overall CI conclusion — red whenever Windows fails — it inspects the triggering run per-job results and publishes only when every job except Windows succeeded. CI stays honestly red on a Windows failure while docs ship from a passing Linux/macOS build.

A `workflow_dispatch` trigger also allows publishing on demand; manual runs skip the CI-jobs gate.

Note: `workflow_run` and `workflow_dispatch` resolve the workflow file from the default branch, so docs publishing activates only once this merges to `main`.

Related to #32

title: Bootstrap resolver tooling and inject rmarkdown for Quarto
description:
Running the resolver required `pak`, `renv`, and `secretbase` to be pre-installed,
and rendering a Quarto document silently relied on `rmarkdown` already being present.
Neither is something the user declares.

`ir` now bootstraps its own resolver tooling and seeds `rmarkdown` for Quarto renders.

## Resolver tooling

On the first resolve for a given R version and platform, the driver installs any
missing `pak`/`renv`/`secretbase` into a dedicated library under the cache
(`<cache>/tooling/<R>-<platform>/`) and prepends it to the resolver session's
library path. Packages already on the user's library path are reused, so existing
setups install nothing. This library is separate from the resolved user library, so
it never collides with a script's own dependency versions. The path is computed in R
from `getRversion()` and `R.version$platform` — no value crosses the Rust/R boundary.

## rmarkdown for Quarto

A Quarto render needs `rmarkdown` for the knitr engine. The resolver injects a bare
`rmarkdown` ref only when the resolved dependency set doesn't already contain it —
whether declared directly or pulled in transitively (e.g. via `quarto`). When
injected, it pulls the latest version (or the latest as of `exclude-newer` when set,
since it resolves against the same snapshot) and prints a one-line advisory to pin a
version. Declaring `rmarkdown` under `ir.dependencies` silences the advisory.

Because a Quarto render can change the resolved set, the resolution cache key folds
in a `quarto` marker (only when true), so non-Quarto runs keep their existing keys.

## Test Plan

End-to-end fixtures in `tests/cli.rs` drive the real resolver and render. No fixture
declares the tooling packages:

- [ ] `run_quarto_fixture_injects_rmarkdown_and_renders` — `report.qmd`, no `rmarkdown`: injected, advisory prints
- [ ] `run_quarto_fixture_with_declared_rmarkdown_skips_injection` — `report-pinned.qmd` declares it: no injection, no advisory
- [ ] `run_quarto_fixture_with_transitive_rmarkdown_skips_advisory` — `report-transitive.qmd` declares `quarto` (Imports rmarkdown): no injection, no advisory
- [ ] `run_quarto_bare_fixture_injects_rmarkdown` — `report-bare.qmd`, no deps at all: still injected, advisory prints

Each fixture asserts the loaded package resolves to `ir`'s run library, not a system copy.

Local rig-managed Windows e2e is blocked by the unrelated `Rscript` `.bat` resolution in #41.

Closes #27

title: Fix Windows cross-drive crash in quarto fixture tests
description:
On windows-latest, un_quarto_fixture_renders_html_with_resolved_packages failed with os error 123: The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect. The runner checks out on D: while the test's temp output dir is on C:, and the two never reproduced together on a single-drive local box.

## Root Cause

Quarto resolves --output-dir relative to the input document's directory, not the cwd. The tests passed an absolute fixture path, so quarto joined the fixture dir with the absolute temp output dir: path.join("D:\...\fixtures\run", "C:\Users\...\Temp\") yields D:\a\ir\ir\tests\fixtures\run\C:\Users\..., which stat rejects. POSIX tolerates the same join (single root), so only the Windows job failed. ir forwards --output-dir verbatim, so this is quarto's path handling, not an ir bug.

## Fix

Set current_dir to the fixture directory and pass just the filename (eport.qmd) as a relative argument, dropping --output-dir. Quarto writes the output beside the input on the same drive, and the path resolution issue disappears on every platform. Applies to both un_quarto_fixture_renders_html_with_resolved_packages and the opt-in un_quarto_selects_requested_r_version.

Verified on Windows: the previously failing test now passes.

This covers one of the three root causes tracked in #46 (the cross-drive join); the

title: Install dev sessioninfo on CI to fix Windows session crash
description:
On `windows-latest`, the fixture tests that resolve dependencies crashed the R session with `0xC0000005` (`ci_dependencies_are_available`, `run_inline_expression_resolves_with_dependencies`, and downstream `tool_install_installs_real_package_entrypoint`).

## Root Cause

sessioninfo's `platform_info()` probes the quarto version with `system2("quarto", env = ...)`. Windows has no `env` program, so the assignment is passed as a command argument and the call faults the session — r-lib/sessioninfo#122. PPM's released `1.2.3` still carries the bug; the fix (r-lib/sessioninfo#123) is only on the development version.

## Fix

Pull `github::r-lib/sessioninfo` in the test job's `setup-r-dependencies` list until a fixed release reaches PPM. The dev version works on every platform, so the install isn't gated to Windows.

Covers the `0xC0000005` root cause tracked in #46. The cross-drive `--output-dir` crash (#52) and reticulate discovery (#48) are handled separately.

Related to #46

title: Fix `ir run` on rig-managed Windows
description:
On a rig-managed Windows machine, `ir run` fails before reaching R, and even with an explicit `--r-version` the `.qmd` render aborts in quarto. Two separate Windows-only bugs (#32).

## Default-R resolution hits the `.bat` shim

With no `--r-version`, resolution falls back to the bare name `Rscript`. On a rig-managed Windows box the only `Rscript` on `PATH` is `Rscript.bat` (from `rig system make-links`), and `std::process::Command` resolves `.exe` only — it won't spawn a `.bat`:

```
could not find `Rscript` on PATH. Install R, or set IR_RSCRIPT to its path.
```

The default install's real `Rscript.exe` is now resolved from `rig list --json` (`"default": true` → its `binary`), the same mechanism the `--r-version` path already uses. `IR_RSCRIPT` stays the top override; non-rig systems and Unix fall back to bare `Rscript` unchanged.

## Canonicalised script paths break quarto

The script path was canonicalised for CWD-independence. On Windows `fs::canonicalize` returns a `\\?\C:\...` verbatim path that Rscript tolerates but quarto's Deno `expandGlobSync` cannot stat:

```
ERROR: (os error 123): stat '\\?\C:\Users\...\e2e.qmd'
```

The path is now passed through untouched. R and quarto both inherit `ir`'s working directory, so a relative path resolves exactly as the user typed it — no canonicalisation, no verbatim prefix. An existence check keeps the clear "cannot read script" error.

Verified locally on a rig-managed Windows box: a default-R `.R` run and a `--r-version` `.qmd` render both succeed with the fixes.

Fixes #32

title: Refactor CLI tests to use real end-to-end fixtures
description:
**Summary**
- Replaces mocked CLI coverage with end-to-end tests that exercise the public `ir` surface against real R scripts and Quarto documents.
- Adds fixture scripts and documents that print concrete markers for package resolution, isolated libraries, Quarto rendering, reticulate, and first-YAML-document parsing.

**Notes**

- Internal-only test scaffolding was removed rather than preserved behind mocks.

title: Add --isolated flag to ir run
description:
Closed #16.

## What

Adds `--isolated` to `ir run`. It runs the user code against **only** the resolved library and base R, dropping the user and site libraries:

```console
$ ir run --isolated script.R
$ ir run --isolated --with cli -e 'cli::cli_alert_success("hi")'
```

By default the resolved library is *prepended* to `.libPaths()` and the user's own libraries stay on as a fallback; `--isolated` removes them so undeclared `library()` calls fail loudly instead of silently borrowing a package the script never declared.

## How

`--isolated` is parsed as an `ir`-level flag (like `-e`/`--with`) and is **not** forwarded to Rscript. For the run phase it points `R_LIBS_USER` and `R_LIBS_SITE` at the resolved library, so `.libPaths()` de-duplicates them away — leaving just the resolved library (via `R_LIBS`) and base R.

Notably, **unsetting** those variables does *not* work: when they are absent R synthesises its *default* user/site library locations and adds them, re-introducing the very library we want gone. With no resolved library (a dependency-free run), both fall back to a never-created path, which R prunes.

Only the run phase is affected — the resolver keeps full access to the user's `pak`/`renv`.

### Caveat

A user `.Renviron` is read *before* `.libPaths()` is built, so if it sets `R_LIBS_USER`/`R_LIBS_SITE`/`R_LIBS` itself, those still take effect (the same caveat the README already notes for the default `R_LIBS` prepend). Combine `--isolated` with `--vanilla` for a fully hermetic run.

## Changes

- `src/main.rs` — flag parsing, threading to `run_script`, the isolation env vars, help text, doc comments.
- `tests/cli.rs` — two new tests (resolved-library de-dup path + no-library fallback) and updated USAGE assertions.
- `tests/snapshots/{help,run-help}.stdout` — regenerated.
- `README.md` — Phase 2 note + new "Isolated runs" section, including the `.Renviron` caveat.

## Testing

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` (24 CLI tests + the R resolution suite) all pass. Also verified end-to-end against real R that a populated user library is dropped only under `--isolated`.

title: Move resolver dependencies to stdin
description:
## Summary
- Parse script YAML in Rust with `saphyr`, then send only dependency specs to the R resolver on stdin, one per line.
- Keep the R side focused on resolution and cache handling, with `readLines(stdin())` as the dependency input path.
- Update docs and tests to cover the new resolver protocol and preserve the existing user-facing behavior.

## Testing
- `cargo test`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: Exec into Rscript for the final run on Unix; add cross-platform CI
description:
## Summary

The user-script run is `ir`'s last action, so on Unix it now **`exec`s into Rscript** instead of spawning a child and waiting:

- R takes over `ir`'s process image, inheriting its PID, stdio and signals directly.
- R's exit status propagates to our caller verbatim — **including death by signal**, which the previous spawn+wait path flattened to `1` (via `status.code().unwrap_or(1)`).
- One fewer process in the tree; no post-R cleanup is needed here.

`exec` is Unix-only, so Windows keeps the existing spawn+wait fallback. Phase 1 (dependency resolution) and `cache dir` still spawn children, since `ir` must continue running afterward.

## Tests

`tests/cli.rs` is now Windows-aware:

- `write_executable` does the `chmod` only under `#[cfg(unix)]`; portable tests (`--version`, `--help`, error cases, `cache` commands) now build and run on Windows.
- The `#!/bin/sh`-fake tests are gated to `#[cfg(unix)]`.
- New `run_propagates_user_script_exit_code` — paired by platform (sh + `exec` on Unix, `.cmd` + spawn+wait on Windows), asserting the script's exit code surfaces unchanged.
- New `run_propagates_user_script_signal_death` (Unix only) — asserts a SIGKILLed script is reported as `signal() == Some(9)`, `code() == None`. This fails without `exec`, so it pins the new behavior.

## CI

New `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

- `test` matrix on **ubuntu / macos / windows**, so the Windows spawn+wait path (no `exec` equivalent, not runnable locally on Unix) is exercised on every push.
- R installed via `r-lib/actions/setup-r` + `setup-r-dependencies` (pak, cached library). Deps are listed explicitly since the repo has no `DESCRIPTION`, so the resolution suite in `tests/test-resolve.R` runs rather than skipping.
- A `rustfmt + clippy` lint job.

## Verified locally

- `cargo test` green on macOS (exit code `42` and signal `137`/SIGKILL propagation confirmed end-to-end).
- `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` clean (Windows path compiles).
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

The Windows test's runtime assertion and the `setup-r-dependencies`-without-`DESCRIPTION` install will get their first real exercise from this PR's CI run.

title: Remove custom dependency version constraints
description:
## Summary

Remove ir's custom upper-bound dependency resolver while keeping dependency specs close to pip/uv-style syntax where pak can support it directly.

## Public-facing changes

- `pkg>=1.0` remains supported as a shorthand for pak's native lower-bound ref.
- `pkg==1.2` is supported as the user-facing exact-pin syntax.
- Native pak refs are still passed through unchanged, but `pkg@version` is no longer foregrounded in docs or examples.
- Upper-bound and exclusion syntax, such as `pkg<=1.2` and `pkg!=1.2`, is not resolved by `ir`.

## Internal-only changes

- Deleted the `pak::pkg_history` based resolver and numeric version selection logic.
- Simplified resolver tests to cover pak ref normalisation and pass-through behavior.

## Testing

- `Rscript -e 'source("driver/resolve.R"); stopifnot(identical(ir_to_ref("pkg==1.2"), "pkg@1.2")); stopifnot(identical(ir_to_ref("pkg>=1.2"), "pkg@>=1.2")); stopifnot(identical(ir_to_ref("pkg!=1.2"), "pkg!=1.2")); stopifnot(identical(ir_to_ref("pkg<=1.2"), "pkg<=1.2"))'`
- `cargo test`
- `git diff --check`

title: Daily resolution cache, located via tools::R_user_dir
description:
Makes repeat `ir run`s of an unchanged script skip pak entirely.

- **Resolution cache:** key = hash(declared deps + today's date + R version/platform) → materialised library path. An identical request the same day reuses its library and never invokes pak; folding in the date forces a fresh resolution at most once a day.
- **Cache location:** defaults to `tools::R_user_dir("ir", "cache")` (honours `R_USER_CACHE_DIR`; `IR_CACHE_DIR` still overrides). The driver computes the cache itself, so the Rust side no longer determines, creates, or passes it.

Tested: 6 Rust + 67 R (testthat) assertions pass.

title: Replace prototype with alt implementation: thin Rust, resolution in R
description:
An alternative take on ir's architecture. Because it branched from an
independent root, it shares no history with the current main prototype —
so this replaces main's tree rather than merging into it. The graft keeps
both histories intact.

Same uv-style goal — self-contained R scripts declaring inline
dependencies — split differently between Rust and R. The Rust binary stays
thin (~210 lines, no crate dependencies); all resolution and
materialisation lives in a single R driver (driver/resolve.R):

- Frontmatter parsed as real YAML with yaml12.
- Dependencies resolved to a transitive closure with pak (pkg_deps).
- Resolved set + R version + platform hashed with secretbase::sha256 into a
  content-addressed library path.
- renv::use installs into renv's cache and materialises a symlink library
  that persists across runs and is shared between scripts resolving to the
  same set.

The script then runs under Rscript --vanilla with .libPaths() pinned to
exactly [materialised library, base R], so nothing leaks from the user's
personal or site libraries.

Dependency specs supported: bare name, >=, <=, <, >, ==. >= goes to pak's
solver natively; the others resolve against published versions
(pak::pkg_history, incl. CRAN archive) and pin the newest match.

The branch is fast-forwardable onto main. Merge with "Rebase and merge" (or
an admin fast-forward) to keep all 5 commits; avoid "Squash", which would
discard the per-commit history.

Prototype by @shikokuchuo.
